title: Power Systems Engineer TIPM, Global Energy, sustainability, and Automation
description:
We are seeking a Power Systems Engineer to support electrical reliability, safety, and regulatory programs across Amazon's North American operations network. This role will be responsible for managing the five-year arc flash study refresh program, performing technical quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of power system studies using SKM Power*Tools, and managing the electrical Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) program across North American facilities.
This position requires a strong understanding of industrial MV and LV power distribution systems. The successful candidate will combine technical engineering expertise with program management capabilities to improve electrical system reliability, reduce operational risks, and maintain electrical safety standards across a large portfolio of operating facilities.
This role requires 50% or more travel to operational facilities across North America to perform technical assessments, investigate equipment reliability issues, validate engineering studies, and support electrical safety program implementation.
Key job responsibilities
Arc Flash Study Refresh Program
- Manage the five-year arc flash study refresh program across North American facilities, ensuring timely completion and alignment with applicable electrical safety standards - across 200+ facilities annually.
- Maintain study inventories, track refresh schedules, and prioritize facilities based on electrical system changes, risk, and program requirements.
- Coordinate with third-party engineering firms and site teams to collect and validate electrical system data.
- Review study deliverables, identify deficiencies and NEC violations, propose appropriate cost-effective resolutions, and track corrective actions through closure, including arc flash labeling, relay/breaker settings adjustment, equipment replacement, and documentation updates.
- Establish program performance metrics and reporting to track study completion, deficiencies, and overall program health.
- Perform root cause analysis (RCA) and develop corrective and preventive actions to address equipment failures and recurring reliability concerns.
- Investigate electrical equipment failures, recurring faults, protective device misoperations, and power distribution system reliability issues.
Power Systems Studies and Technical QA/QC
- Perform detailed technical QA/QC of power system studies using SKM Power*Tools, including short-circuit, protective device coordination, arc flash, and load flow analyses.
- Independently review and validate SKM models, study assumptions, equipment parameters, protective device settings, and engineering calculations.
- Identify modeling errors, inconsistencies, and technical deficiencies in studies submitted by external engineering consultants.
- Verify study results against applicable IEEE, NFPA, and other relevant engineering standards.
- Review engineering recommendations related to protective device coordination, incident energy reduction, equipment ratings, and electrical system reliability.
- Document QA/QC findings, coordinate corrections with engineering consultants, and verify resolution before accepting final study deliverables.
- Develop and maintain standardized study review checklists, technical acceptance criteria, and QA/QC processes.

title: Principal Engineer:  Annapurna Labs Training and Inference , Annapurna Labs, AWS Neuron SDK
description:
At Amazon, Principal Engineers are both technical leaders and hands-on builders. As Amazon's most senior individual contributors, Principal Engineers work on our hardest problems, help establish technical standards, and drive the overall technical architecture, engineering practices, and methodologies for products that delight our customers. On the AWS Neuron SDK team within Annapurna Labs, that mandate is AI model performance on Amazon's custom silicon.
We are looking for a Principal Engineer to drive AI model performance across the lifecycle on AWS Trainium — pre-training, post-training and alignment, and inference serving — with deep hands-on expertise in one of these areas and the drive to influence across all three. Neuron is Amazon's software stack: the layer between customer ML frameworks and Trainium / Inferentia silicon. The responsibilities are broad: you will have the opportunity to drive deeply into model enablement across the path from a model's first pre-training step through aligned post-training to cost- and latency-optimized serving at scale.
You will drive performance for a wide range of AI models, including the leading open-source models and direct collaborations with foundation-model developers, as well as supporting Amazon's own internal model development initiatives. This is a deep hands-on builder role: you will write code, own the forward and backward path, and make binding technical decisions, while influencing direction across the broader Neuron organization, partner teams (EC2, EKS, VPC, Bedrock, HyperPod), and leading ML customers. Annapurna offers full-stack ownership — chip to server to network to compiler to cloud — so you see your work run at customer scale, something that doesn't exist at a standalone chip company or startup. Over time, this person ends up owning the whole process end-to-end.
Key job responsibilities
As the Principal Engineer for Annapurna Labs Training and Inference, you will bring deep hands-on expertise in one of the following areas and influence across all three:
Pre-Training Performance
●Kernel optimization for ML training — forward and backward path — and drive performance out of it, with training collective algorithms (collectives, all-reduce, cross-accelerator coordination) as the primary source of gains.
●Prove top-tier performance even at small scale, and clear the path so customers can land AI models on the chip out of the box. This is a performance role, not an Applied Science role — you partner with scientists but own making it fast, not making it correct.
Post-Training & Alignment
●Supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and alignment stack that turns pretrained base models into production-grade, aligned models on Trainium — the main lever on delivered model quality and the fastest-growing, least-covered workload class on Trainium today.
●Deliver first-class RLHF/RLAIF and preference methods (PPO, GRPO, DPO/IPO/KTO, reward modeling) with training-plus-inference co-location and convergence safeguards (KL control, reward-scaling, policy-collapse detection), and native performance for the post-training ecosystem (TRL, veRL, NeMo-Aligner, TorchTitan/TorchAO, JAX).
Inference / Serving
●Inference optimization strategy within the Neuron SDK — adapting inference algorithms to Trainium's unique architecture to unlock performance existing industry approaches leave on the table, and maximizing the chip's compute and memory bandwidth to drive cost and latency improvements for large-scale model serving.
●Influence hardware-software co-design by partnering with Annapurna's chip architecture teams so future silicon incorporates lessons from production model serving.
Influence across all three
●Serve as a technical leader on demanding, cross-functional projects spanning pre-training, post-training, and inference; functionally decompose complex problems into simple, straightforward solutions.
●Exert technical influence across multiple teams, mentor senior engineers, and raise the technical bar across the organization.
●Balance technical leadership with strong business judgment to make the right technology choices.

The AWS Neuron team builds the software stack — compiler, runtime, and ML frameworks — that powers Amazon's Trainium and Inferentia accelerators in EC2 Trn1/2 and Inf1 servers. description:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a high-impact Principal Product Manager with a deep specialization in mechanical infrastructure to define and execute the product strategy for our next-generation infrastructure and facility systems. AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
As a Principal Mechanical Product Manager you will be responsible for defining the "what" and "why" of our mechanical strategy, ensuring alignment across cross-functional teams, and driving critical decisions even in the face of complexity or resistance. The leader in this role has the ability to make tough calls, stand behind decisions, and navigate obstacles. You must be comfortable pushing back on stakeholders and driving alignment.
You are the voice of the business at the front of the pipeline — the person who decides which platforms earn the organization’s capacity, and why. You own the customer need each platform serves, its system-level requirements, and how it fits into the broader roadmap. You own the technical requirements strategy that sets the foundation for timing, cost, and execution. You own the mechanism by which field, cost, and customer signals are collected, converted into requirements for a new platform or its next revision, and prioritized against everything else in the portfolio. You bring rigor to the front end so that platforms enter the pipeline with validated business requirements, clear boundaries, and a defensible priority.

- System-Level Ownership: Own and understand how mechanical designs impact the broader infrastructure (e.g., cooling, electrical, structural). Evaluate how new business requests affect the entire fleet and propose integrated solutions.
- Product Strategy & Roadmap: Define and communicate a multi-year vision, strategy, and product roadmap for advanced mechanical infrastructure products. Coordinate between multiple teams to develop compelling business cases to substantiate business value, define product prioritization, and outline budget and resources required to implement product roadmaps.
- Modular Standardization: Standardize complex mechanical systems into modular, prefabricated skids to compress on-site data center construction and commissioning timelines.

- Strategic Alignment & Vision: Lead the definition of challenges at the facility and product levels. Ensure all stakeholders are aligned on the path forward, particularly when navigating complex transitions.
- Value Engineering & Decision Making: Actively challenge existing assumptions regarding cost and complexity.
- Technical Leadership: Serve as a subject matter expert who can evaluate technical trade-offs.
- Systems Thinking: Ability to see the big picture and understand the upstream/downstream impacts of mechanical design choices on electrical and structural systems.
A day in the life
Your day moves between signal and strategy. You might begin by synthesizing customer needs and cost data into a sharpened requirement for a platform’s next revision, then join a pre-production readiness review where you and a Principal Engineer pressure-test whether an existing product can serve a new customer need or whether a new variant is truly justified. Your internal stakeholders span the full lifecycle: Principal Engineers, TPMs, product team, engineering, sourcing, industrialization and construction partners. title: Product Design Engineer II, AMXL WIDE
description:
Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) is a single-threaded organization with ownership of the end-to-end customer experience for large, heavy, and bulky products. AMXL consolidates the complete supply chain including strategy, data analytics, technology, operations, warehousing, order fulfillment, transportation, and delivery. AMXL also offers special handling services such as Room of Choice delivery, Haul-Away, and Installation/Assembly for select items. AMXL currently operates in North America, Europe, Japan, and India with plans for further expansion.
We are seeking a highly skilled and results-driven Design Engineer to join our dynamic AMXL Worldwide Industrial Design Engineering (WIDE) team. In this critical role, you will drive analysis, design, and deployment of high-impact retrofit programs and process re-engineering projects for AMXL Fulfillment Centers, Delivery Stations, and Sort Centers. The individual will primarily own the capacity models for Last Mile and will help improve and automate the model refreshes going into organizational quarterly guidance and planning cycles. Additionally, the role requires driving concept designs that enhance our customer and associate experience by introducing new capabilities and re-engineering processes while increasing the overall safety and efficiency of our operations.
We are looking for someone who possesses a blend of customer-facing and technical skills and will own retrofit programs and projects from ideation through execution and validation. Successful candidates will possess a strong background in facility design, material handling equipment, automation, and process engineering with a blend of deep skills in program managing complex projects, strong technical aptitude, troubleshooting capabilities, and customer-facing skills, along with a passion for innovating and simplifying processes. You are able to work successfully across multiple large engineering and operations teams at a strategic level and at an operations integration level.
Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end process design and site layout creation for each new business initiative and process improvement/re-engineering project in delivery station and sort center network
- Own the capacity models for LM BU.
- Determine all resources required for each retrofit project in terms of site layout, traffic plans, optimal material flow, equipment specification, and operations scheduling/ops clock
- Consolidate all retrofit efforts from change management to post-launch support for each site to streamline launch work, minimize disruption, and reduce launch costs
- Collaborate with internal teams and external vendors to generate high quality, cost effective solutions in very short periods of time
- Simultaneously manage multiple high visibility projects and tasks while effectively influencing, negotiating, and communicating with internal and external business partners, contractors and vendors
- Cross-pollinate best practices between engineering and operations teams.
- Provide technical leadership for large-scale engineering projects
- Lead ergonomic design improvements leveraging ergonomics, safety, and field ACES team resources
- With each retrofit, drive standardization, documentation of core design and process elements for scalable network growth across North America Logistics using strong process management and Lean principles
- Own and deliver on post-launch reviews and customer feedback, and incorporate feedback into future project plans
A day in the life
The role will require daily interactions with Operations, Safety, Process/Design Engineering, Launch, Finance, Supply Chain Execution, and Planning teams to ensure delivery station and sort center retrofit programs are well-defined in terms of aligning on the launch calendar, determining capacity requirements, identifying resources, clarifying roles and responsibilities, and leading the change management process. The role needs to have a deep understanding on both business needs and operational standards to be able translate business inputs to operational designs and operational constraints into business plans. There will be daily/weekly calls with Design and Launch teams to review retrofit designs and to collaborate with business/program owners to ensure the success of strategic initiatives implemented on time at the highest quality. Once a retrofit is completed and handed over to Launch/Startup teams, the role requires documentation of these changes and updates in respective capacity management systems with follow ups on the approval chains with Ops and Business leaders.

The Propulsion Lab Engineer will be a key member of Amazon Leo's Propulsion Manufacturing team, combining deep technical expertise with strong collaborative skills. This role will lead the development and optimization of electric propulsion manufacturing infrastructure while working across engineering disciplines. The ideal candidate will drive technical solutions for manufacturing challenges, implement process controls, and maintain critical lab equipment, while effectively partnering with Design, Quality, Systems, and Test engineers to translate requirements into robust manufacturing processes. • Build or Test development and production hardware in accordance with SOPs, work instructions, and engineering drawings, including component and subsystem fabrication (machining, 3D printing, rapid prototyping).
• Conduct detailed inspections and testing of production and reworked hardware to validate functionality, performance, and conformance to specifications.
• Navigate MES/SAP systems in support of production operations.
• Execute failure analysis and root cause investigations on non-conforming propulsion hardware.
• Execute hardware rework tasks as needed.

• Identify and/or lead process improvement initiatives to increase rework efficiency, reduce scrap rates, maintain 5S standards and improve first-pass yield.
• Collaborate with engineering teams to resolve integration challenges, validate rework procedures, provide design-for-manufacturability feedback, and implement corrective actions.
• Support the development and improvement of assembly and test procedures based on hands-on build experience and design-for-manufacturability feedback.

• Support and maintain Test and/or Mfg. team tool program for development and production stations.
• Collaborate with Amazon Leo facility team and support preventative maintenance for development and production test chambers.
• Support with Propulsion lab organization and floor space layout.

• Train and mentor team members on rework techniques, lab systems, tools, safety protocols, and quality standards.

- • Experience in hardware design and validation of components, subsystems, and systems.

- • Experience with precision torque, measurement, and inspection devices (e.g., automated and manual torque wrenches, calipers, micrometers, profilometers, optical inspection devices, multi-meters).

- • Demonstrated troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.

- • Experience with test execution software such as Test Stand, LabVIEW, and Python.

You will be responsible for improving the health and safety of our data centers, advancing safety culture, and protecting our employees. Each day you will work with our data center engineers, the people who make the cloud go. They are working with electrical switching equipment, large scale air handling mechanical systems, and critical IT gear.
You will work closely with experts in security, construction, operations, logistics, compliance, corporate counsel, and human resources to further the global health safety program. You will partner with employees as well as contractors to achieve health and safety goals and improve our already strong safety culture. You will work in a fast-paced environment where our operations are rapidly changing, advocating safe changes in the face of new infrastructure, new tools, and new products/processes.
This role is for a qualified and experienced people leader. The primary responsibilities of the role are to own the safety strategy for a multi-cluster portfolio of Texas data centers and to manage a team of Health and Safety Managers across those sites. You will set the vision and define the safety strategy for your regional portfolio, design the right team structure and mechanisms to meet long-term business goals, and achieve consensus on priorities with senior operations partners. The Texas portfolio is in a period of rapid growth, with new launches and some of the organization's largest builds, so you will anticipate future growth and investment needs and build a workforce strategy to match.
You will have managed a team of safety professionals and will be able to demonstrate how you improved the performance of an existing team along with displaying skills in creating or growing a team. You will manage succession planning, hiring, coaching, managing performance, and promoting. You will be knowledgeable in US occupational safety regulations, including OSHA recordkeeping requirements (29 CFR 1904), as well as industry best practices related to hazard recognition and mitigation in critical infrastructure environments.
You will be part of a regional and global team that works with internal and external partners to maintain and enhance the safety of operations. Close collaboration with onsite physical security, vendors, compliance officers, risk management, and fire/life safety systems is required. Additionally, you will work with employees and contractors to achieve specific safety objectives.
You must be an effective communicator, sending clear, concise, and consistent messages verbally, in written form, and in public speaking forums. You will write compelling strategic narratives, including QBR and operating plan inputs, and present them effectively to Directors and VPs. You will advise, instruct, and train company safety professionals, as well as operations personnel, on safety policies and procedures. title: Reliability Engineer, Amazon Leo
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Reliability Engineer to drive design for reliability in Amazon Leo hardware systems. This role will be responsible for developing and leading various reliability activities during product development and through the life of the product. It will require interfacing closely with subsystem teams, providing technical input and guidance on designs, and supporting as needed for reliability analysis and testing.
The ideal candidate will have experience in using Physics-of-Failure based models to develop and implement both analytical and empirical solutions for product quality/reliability risk identification and assessment during the product design, manufacturing, testing and deployment stages. The candidate should be able to drive Amazon Leo's requirements by carrying out stress driven risk analysis, including thermal, electrical and mechanical stresses in order to identify over-stress and fatigue-related product weaknesses. They should also be comfortable in assessing electronics manufacturing process related quality/reliability issues.
At the component level, the individual will drive critical component identification, support vendor selection and define component qualification requirements. The candidate will also be expected to use their knowledge of PCBA manufacturing, electronic component derating, as well as system-level performance requirements to establish critical quality and reliability metrics.
At the system level, the candidate will support development of system level reliability models and perform reliability assessments and risk analyses for optimization of design. The candidate will be also be expected to be familiar with system reliability engineering tools, such as reliability block diagram, statistical modeling and on orbit data analytics.
Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
- Assist with building a center of excellence for reliability analysis and testing
- Develop HALT, HASS and accelerated life test campaigns
- Define sample sizes and test specifications to demonstrate target reliability and confidence numbers
- Develop subsystem reliability models and establish reliability allocations across components to meet reliability targets.
- Review, guide, and support subsystem team component selections, derating and FMEAs
- Support component and manufacturing process qualification
- Drive root cause investigation and failure analysis for hardware failures
Basic qualifications: - Experience in developing functional specifications, design verification plans and functional test procedures
- Bachelor's degree or above in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
- 3+ years of experience in hardware reliability engineering, preferably with a focus on satellite systems or space applications.
- Knowledge of reliability engineering principles, methods, and tools.
- Knowledge of environmental testing
- Proficiency in failure analysis techniques and materials characterization methods.
- Familiarity with electronics (PCBs, PCBAs, electronic components) and moving mechanical assemblies.
Preferred qualifications: - Master's or Doctorate degree or above in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
- Experience with environmental testing, including temperature cycling, vibration, highly accelerated limit testing (HALT), and highly-accelerated stress screening (HASS).
- Basic knowledge of PCB fabrication, SMT, and polymerics application manufacturing processes.
- Familiarity with relevant industry standards, including IPC, JEDEC, AIAA, AEC, MIL, and SMC standards.

description:
Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building revolutionary robotic systems that combine frontier AI, sophisticated control systems, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation solutions capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.
As a Robotics Electrical Engineer II in our team, you will be responsible for supporting product development functions across design, validation and manufacturing. We are looking for candidates who thrive in a fast-paced start-up like environment and want to invent the future. In this role, you will wear many hats working on system design down to quick turn prototypes, manufacturing production processes, design validation and debug. You will work at the integrated circuit and product systems level and drive the quality bar to ensure the products we ship are bug free.
To be successful you need to be highly motivated, understand how to solve problems and dive deep while delivering to the highest standards. You will demonstrate a strong working knowledge of product electrical design with expertise in systems integration, the desire to learn from new challenges, and the problem-solving and communication skills to work within a highly interactive and experienced team.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead end-to-end electrical hardware design for robotic systems from system-level architecture and schematic capture through PCB layout, prototyping, and production release
- Own schematic design and multi-layer PCB layout in Altium Designer, including stack-up definition, power delivery, and signal integrity
- Drive Design for Manufacturability (DFM) in collaboration with fabrication and assembly vendors
- Define system-level electrical architecture for robotic platforms encompassing power regulation, motor drive electronics, sensor interfaces, and compute modules
- Contribute embedded firmware to bring up hardware, validate interfaces, and unblock system integration
- Lead troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and redesign of electrical and electromechanical failures across prototype and production builds
- Develop and execute board- and system-level validation test plans
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including controls, mechanical, firmware, and software
A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing motor controller schematics in Altium, refining gate-drive timing for an actuator in a robotic subsystem. After a quick stand-up with the mechanical and firmware teams, you head to the lab to validate a new sensor board, probing communication buses, tuning thresholds, and capturing data for the controls team. The sensor work might involve force feedback one week and depth sensing the next. By afternoon you're debugging a current loop on a prototype joint, flashing firmware tweaks to tighten the servo response, and updating your PCB layout to fix a routing issue found during testing. No two days look the same; you'll move fluidly between board design, bench work, and firmware across a range of robotic sensing and actuation challenges.

title: Senior Data Engineer, AWS Analytics Engineering
description:
The AWS Analytics Engineering (AAE) organization is the analytics backbone of AWS — we build and operate the data platform that powers business decisions across more than 150 AWS services. Every insight surfaced to AWS product leadership, from service adoption trends to revenue drivers, flows through systems our team designs, builds, and maintains.
We operate at massive scale — processing petabytes of data daily through thousands of jobs consisting of transformations, reporting queries, ingestions, and infrastructure management scripts. Our engineers work directly with source systems to procure data, convert it into structured formats, build large-scale processing pipelines, design analytical data models, and maintain infrastructure with the highest security and compliance standards.
We are seeking a Senior Data Engineer to join our team. This individual will own 3-5 data domains end-to-end, operate hundreds of pipelines, and drive architectural improvements that impact how AWS leadership makes decisions. You will partner with service teams across AWS to design data contracts, build ingestion flows, and deliver analytical models that serve the entire organization.
The ideal candidate is a technical leader who thrives in ambiguity, takes a long-term architectural view, and consistently delivers exemplary solutions. You are an expert with SQL, ETL, and data processing, with experience leveraging cloud-based data services such as AWS EMR, Glue, Redshift, and Lambda. The candidate should have hands-on experience with AI/ML technologies, including LLMs, and a strong understanding of designing and building Agentic Frameworks — including autonomous agents, multi-agent orchestration, and tool integration. You are comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment, able to think big while paying careful attention to detail, and passionate about building data platforms using AI to accelerate the next generation of analytics at AWS scale.
Key job responsibilities
Identify limitations and opportunities in data processing tools, drive improvements and innovation, define data processing guidelines, and ensure best practices in all pipelines designed and reviewed. For example: redesigning ingestion frameworks to handle new AWS service telemetry data, or building reusable transformation patterns adopted across multiple teams.
Define and own data architecture at the team level — ensuring architecture effectively matches business problems and data challenges with security, scalability, and cost effectiveness. Show good judgment making technical trade-offs between short-term technology needs and long-term business needs.
Produce exemplary code — solutions that are easily usable by customers, inventive, secure, easily maintainable, appropriately scalable, and extensible. Build solutions that are easy for others to contribute to. Work to simplify, optimize, and remove bottlenecks.
Define and own infrastructure architecture at the team level. Anticipate data management and access patterns, evolve the technology stack to remove bottlenecks, and deliver systems that are secure, scalable, and long lasting. Define team-level guidelines and best practices for infrastructure management and automation.
Solve complex ambiguous problems — for example, designing cross-domain data models that unify billing, usage, and service telemetry data, or combining multiple datasets to solve problems that couldn't be solved before. Spot areas that might lead to customer confusion, data misinterpretation, or gaps in data contracts.
Effectively split project work into parallel tasks that can be performed by themselves and others and reassembled successfully. Drive to completion projects with dependencies on peers or other teams.
Influence related teams' data architecture and software design. Provide technical assessments for promotions. Actively mentor and develop others. Build consensus when confronted with discordant views.
Drive data engineering best practices — Data Discovery, Naming Conventions, Operational Excellence, Data Security. Ensure team's data is auditable, available, and accessible.
Proactively fix data architecture deficiencies and propose larger projects which may require the work of other teams. Drive improvements through code review, design discussions, team planning, and operational reviews.
Participate in on-call rotation and own operational health of data systems — establish monitoring, alarming, runbooks, and SLA tracking. Drive continuous improvement in reliability and incident response.

- Experience in at least one modern scripting or programming language, such as Python, Java, Scala, or NodeJS
- Experience mentoring team members on best practices
- Experience building/operating highly available, distributed systems of data extraction, ingestion, and processing of large data sets
- Experience building data products incrementally and integrating and managing data sets from multiple sources
- Experience communicating with users, other technical teams, and management to collect requirements, describe data modeling decisions and data engineering strategy
- Experience providing technical leadership and mentoring other engineers for best practices on data engineering
- Experience with MPP databases such as Amazon Redshift
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, analytics, mathematics, statistics, IT or equivalent
- 5+ years of data warehouse technical architectures, data modeling, infrastructure components, ETL/ ELT and reporting/analytic tools and environments, data structures and hands-on SQL coding experience
Preferred qualifications: - Experience with big data technologies such as: Hadoop, Hive, Spark, EMR
- Experience operating large data warehouses
- Experience working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage

- Experience with enterprise-scale infrastructure or development-based cloud programs/projects in a related industry

title: Senior Software Development Engineer, Core Search
description:
The Amazon Search Navigation AI team helps customers go from a broad search intent to the few products that fit their needs, so they can make a confident purchase decision. We generate highly relevant, context-aware, and personalized search refinements. We also decide the order they appear in across Amazon's Search Navigation experiences, guiding customers to the most relevant results. The team owns Search Navigation's P0 metrics and defect guardrails, which keep performance and reliability high for hundreds of millions of customers.
We are reinventing search refinement with generative AI. Our recently launched Smart Refinement experience uses large language models (LLMs) served online to turn product specifications into natural-language suggestions that match how customers think, such as "for colder weather" or "lightweight for travel." Each suggestion is personalized to the customer's context. Next, we are building multi-turn, conversational refinement, where each interaction builds on the last and helps customers narrow their intent in fewer steps.
We build and run the engineering systems behind this work, including the Navigation Experience Service (NES). NES connects to Amazon's core search systems, serves more than 3 billion queries worldwide every day, and runs real-time LLM inference at global scale under strict latency and cost limits. Our platform supports launches of new navigation content and UIs, and it makes fast offline and online experimentation possible.
We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to be a technical leader on the team. You will shape the architecture of our Search Navigation platform, including the systems that serve LLMs in real time, lead complex projects that span multiple teams, and work closely with Applied Scientists to take LLM innovations from research into production. You are comfortable with ambiguity, you set a high bar for engineering, and you are curious about applied science.

- Drive the engineering roadmap for Smart Refinement and multi-turn conversational refinement, scaling from initial launch to a much larger share of search traffic
- Build safe, reliable GenAI experiences with layered safeguards: input triggering and exclusion controls, output validation and filtering, and graceful fallbacks
- Partner with Applied Scientists, Product Managers, and Program Managers to define requirements and bring models (including distilled LLMs) into production

title: Senior Sustainability Specialist, AWS Global Sustainability
description:
Join us at the forefront of AWS's sustainability initiatives to work on the advancements that will deliver Amazon's long term worldwide sustainability strategy. At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people.
AWS Global Sustainability (AWSGS) is a team of sustainability experts, scientists, engineers, program strategists, and product managers that deliver on our ambition to reach net-zero carbon by 2040 as part of Amazon’s Climate Pledge, as well as manage and report on our sustainability progress more broadly.
We are looking for a results-oriented Sr. Sustainability Specialist who’s passionate about building decarbonization into core business strategy. You bring deep subject matter expertise in GHG data management and accounting, and a clear point of view on the technologies and innovations needed to scale carbon-free power generation and transition to a net-zero electric grid. You have a demonstrated ability to think strategically about business, technical, and methodological challenges, with the skill set to drive tactical execution across multiple workstreams. You thrive in ambiguity – structuring problems, reaching defensible conclusions, and documenting clearly.
In this role you will engage partner teams across AWS infrastructure teams (energy, real estate, capacity delivery, environmental), to embed carbon-aware decision-making into how current and future AWS data centers are planned, sited, and built. You will work across science, engineering, and reporting teams to strengthen the integrity, granularity, and auditability of AWS's GHG inventory, and will drive the development/adoption of new and improved carbon accounting methods as data and standards continue to mature.

description:
About US
Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) is AWS's fully managed live streaming service, built on the same battle-tested technology that powers Twitch and trusted by thousands of enterprises across gaming, social, live commerce, sports, and entertainment.
Our mission: enable developers to build communities around live video. We handle everything from ingest to processing to delivery at global scale, so developers can focus on creating interactive, engaging live experiences for their audiences. Whether you're streaming to tens of millions of concurrent viewers or just getting started, Amazon IVS removes the complexity so developers can move fast.
About The Role
As a Software Development Engineer on the Amazon IVS Control Plane team, you will build customer-facing experiences and highly scalable, reliable, and secure systems that power Amazon IVS.
The IVS Console is the primary interface through which customers configure, monitor, and manage their IVS resources, while the IVS Control Plane provides the APIs and backend systems that orchestrate those resources at AWS scale. You will work across both to build seamless end-to-end experiences for IVS customers. Your work will directly empower developers, broadcasters, and businesses around the world to deliver low-latency, interactive video experiences.
Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop intuitive user interfaces for the IVS Console using modern web technologies
- Design and develop scalable backend services and public APIs for Amazon IVS
- Build distributed systems that manage the configuration, orchestration, and lifecycle of live video streaming resources using TypeScript, Go or similar modern programming languages
- Define and maintain infrastructure using infrastructure as code practices, primarily with AWS CDK
- Work closely with engineers, product managers, UX designers, and applied scientists to deliver seamless customer experiences
- Ensure systems are highly available, scalable, and secure at AWS scale
- Apply engineering best practices across testing, performance optimization, observability, and code quality
- Collaborate with other AWS teams to integrate shared services and deliver consistent customer experiences across AWS services
- Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, design reviews, and on-call rotations
- Drive operational excellence through automation, metrics, alarms, and runbooks
A day in the life
You might start the morning by checking how the service is running and investigating an issue that surfaced overnight. Later, you could join a design discussion for a new customer feature, thinking through the experience from the public API, console, all the way to the backend systems that make it work. After lunch, you might work through an interesting technical problem with a teammate, review a change, or meet with product to refine how a feature should work for customers. Some days are focused on building intuitive customer experiences, while others take you deep into distributed systems and large scale service operations. You’ll have the opportunity to follow problems across the stack and see the features you build through from idea to launch.

- Experience with frontend security best practices

description:
At Amazon Web Services (AWS), Security is our highest priority. AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) is accountable for the end to end vulnerability lifecycle across all of AWS: finding, contextualizing, and assessing vulnerabilities, and driving remediation at machine speed, without manual work from builders and at the lowest cost to AWS.
The Remediation Engineering Team (PitCrew) builds and operates the capabilities that close the gap between a finding being known and it being gone. Our mandate is to automate mitigation, remediation, and assessment. We develop capabilities for mitigation and remediation outside of patching: recognizing potentially vulnerable and unused software components and retiring them on behalf of service teams, delivering remediations to builders as changes they can review and approve, and acting on hosts and their payloads within minutes when a patch is unavailable or too slow. We also build the tooling AVM security engineers use to codify, classify, and track the blockers that keep service teams from remediating on time, and the automation behind assessment and attestation: contextualizing findings with asset-level signals such as network reachability and compensating controls so that severity reflects true risk and every critical finding is a true critical, attesting to accepted residual risk, and generating evidence of those decisions continuously for auditors and customers.
As a Software Development Engineer II on PitCrew, you will design, build, and operate services that act on hosts and containers across AWS at fleet scale. You will own features end to end: working with security engineers to understand a problem, writing the design, implementing it, deploying it, and operating what you ship. The work sits at the intersection of distributed systems, host and container internals, and security, and much of it is about making changes to production systems safely and reversibly at scale.

- Design, implement, and operate services and automation that mitigate, remediate, and assess vulnerabilities across AWS fleets, reducing the attack surface and mean time to remediate without a human in the loop.
- Build the contextualization that turns raw findings into accurate, prioritized risk for builders, so service teams act on true criticals first.
- Own the full lifecycle of your software: requirements, design reviews, implementation, testing, deployment, metrics, alarms, and on-call.
- Build tooling that security engineers use daily, and work closely with them to turn investigation, remediation, assessment, and attestation workflows into software.
- Make changes to production hosts and containers safe by default: reversible, observable, attested, and gated appropriately.

title: Software Development Engineer, Building Connectivity Engineering
description:
Every Amazon data center runs on networks no customer ever sees: the corporate network that engineers and tools use to reach the fleet, the segmented networks that cameras and badge readers ride on, the network for building systems, and the isolated controls networks behind power and cooling. Building Connectivity Engineering (BCE), part of AWS Networking, owns the design and operation of those fabrics in every Amazon data center, and builds them into more than 100 new sites a year. Building Connectivity Software Systems (BCSS) is the software team inside BCE.
We build the controller for these networks. It holds the intended state of every fabric as a model, computes everything a new site needs (addresses, routing identifiers, ports, cabling, device registration) before a technician plugs in the first rack, renders device configuration from the model, and drives the deployment and monitoring platforms that AWS Networking already runs. The first production release went live in September 2026 and took a site build that used to need about twenty hand-run steps down to one request. Most of the controller is still ahead of us.
We are hiring Software Development Engineers to build the next releases: a versioned model of intended network state with full history and rollback, device configuration rendered from that model instead of written by hand, and the orchestration that takes a site from a plan to live traffic with one physical touch. You will design services, write the design documents for them, build them on AWS, prove them in shadow mode against real sites, and run them in production. The network engineers who hold the fabric knowledge are your partners; your code is the engine their models run on.
Key job responsibilities
* Design and build services in AWS (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CDK), modeled with Smithy and deployed through pipelines you own.
* Write the design document for what you build. Every engineer on this team writes designs; it is a core part of the job, and seniority is not the gate.
* Integrate with the systems of record in AWS Networking (IP address management, device registry, routing-policy store, configuration store and release, deployment, cabling plans), and find out what each contract actually does, against the real service, before committing to a date.
* Prove correctness in shadow mode: compute what the automation would do for a site, diff it against what engineers did by hand, and get to zero discrepancies before any cutover.
* Own what you ship in production: metrics, alarms, runbooks, and a turn in the team's on-call rotation, which covers the new services and the ones the team inherited.
* Keep fabric knowledge out of the code. New fabrics, site types and rack types arrive as models the network engineers author; your job is to make the second one cost a configuration change.
* Estimate honestly: size work by how novel it is and how many systems outside the team it touches, raise partner asks early, and say what is unknown.
A day in the life
You pick up a card to add a new reservation type to the allocation service. Before writing code you spend an hour against the real partner API in a test account and find that the contract does not do what its wiki page says, so you write that down, re-size the card, and raise the ask with the partner team that morning instead of three weeks in. The afternoon is a design review of a teammate's state machine change, where the question you keep asking is what happens on the retry, and your own code review landing with its shadow-mode diff attached. A few times a year you are the on-call engineer for a week, and the team expects that week to be your work.
About the team
BCSS, formed in May 2026. We bring software engineering practice to a problem space that has not had software developers, and we never cut corners: slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Our stance in one line is a team tenet: we don't just make a change, we make a changer. Our software runs on AWS and operates entirely detached from production data traffic.
We work inside an operating model where network fabric teams run like software teams: they own their business logic, expose APIs, and measure outcomes. BCSS builds the software; every fabric team owns its automation roadmap and its adoption. Design reviews are open and argued; the best objection in the room wins, whoever raised it.

- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Preferred qualifications: - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Experience architecting/operating solutions built on AWS
- Experience owning and leading significant projects from concept to deployment
- Experience working with networking fundamentals or Internet protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, SSL, DNS, HTTP/S, or equivalent
- Experience with workflow orchestration and event-driven designs (Step Functions, EventBridge or equivalents), including idempotency, retries and rollback
- Experience integrating with systems whose APIs you do not control, and designing for their failure modes
- Experience with data modeling: versioned data, graph-shaped data, or generating configuration or code from a model

title: Software Development Manager, EBS Server Agility
description:
If leading a team that builds secure, autonomous systems to test, deploy, and patch server software for one of the world's largest storage services excites you, the EBS Server Agility team is the place to do it. EBS is a foundational AWS service on which most other AWS services depend, and our teams build and operate the Continuous Integration platform and the deployment and patching infrastructure that keep EBS server software fast to ship, current, and secure across 400,000 bare-metal servers, infrastructure that serves millions of AWS customers and exabytes of data every day.
We are looking for a Software Development Manager to lead an engineering team in our DevOps space. This is the space that spans Continuous Integration, which builds the platform that decides whether a change is safe to ship, and Deployments and Patching, which safely rolls that change out to a stateful storage engine serving live customer I/O. Both sit in the critical path for feature velocity and security compliance, and both are places where strong engineering leadership has outsized impact.
You will not be writing the code or designing the systems yourself. You will lead the engineers who do: hiring and growing the team, setting clear technical direction, removing ambiguity, and delivering results predictably. You will decide where your systems sit in their lifecycle, define goals tied to business needs, and build the mechanisms that let the team deliver consistently without wearing out its best people. The guiding philosophy is simple and demanding: every manual step in the operator path is a defect in the system, and your team builds the test frameworks, CI infrastructure, and deployment services that engineer that toil away.
Server CI and deployment at EBS shape how the software evolves to support new hardware platforms, new partitions (including edge and Outpost), and new operational models. You will partner with principal engineers and leaders across EC2 and EBS, and represent your team's work in discussions that shape how EBS evolves. If you want your leadership to have real impact at AWS scale, and you are excited by building a team that builds systems that test, deploy, and patch themselves, we would love to talk to you.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead, hire, develop, and promote a team of software engineers (up to Senior SDE, L6) across the CI and Deployments domains, building a team with sustainable on-call and clear growth paths
- Own and set the technical direction and roadmap across both the CI platform and the deployment and patching systems, and be accountable for how they work together
- Deliver a CI platform that answers "is this change safe to deploy to 400,000 servers," including distributed test orchestration, intelligent test selection, and observability across x86 and Graviton
- Deliver deployment pipelines and automated security patching that safely update a stateful storage engine across all AWS regions and partitions with zero customer impact and manifest consistency on a biweekly cadence
- Drive toward secure, autonomous operations: automated canary analysis, rollback, anomaly detection, and self-healing automation that takes the operator out of the loop
- Own operational health across both domains: on-call, patch compliance, and the cadences that keep the fleet green
- Define goals tied to business needs and deliver them predictably, building mechanisms so the team ships consistently
- Lead the team through change with clarity and empathy, and influence technical direction beyond your immediate team
A day in the life
Your day moves across many disparate topics. You might align the team on a roadmap for the quarter, coach an engineer through a design, review progress against goals, and make a principled call that trades a little speed for safety on a change headed to the fleet. You will remove blockers, set priorities, and keep on-call sustainable while the team ships. You will partner with principal engineers and leaders across EBS and EC2, and you will represent your team's work to senior leadership.
This is a high-visibility role. The work in this space affects every EBS customer, and your team's output is regularly reviewed by senior leadership. You will collaborate across organizational boundaries, influence technical direction beyond your immediate team, and build a team that is better for your presence but does not need you to be successful.
We value managers who lead through ambiguity, reduce toil through smart automation, make principled tradeoffs between speed and safety, hire and grow strong engineers, and elevate everyone around them.
About the team
EBS Server Agility is the DevOps space for EBS Server, owning the Continuous Integration platform and the server deployment and patching infrastructure. Our engineers build distributed test orchestration and qualification systems, deployment pipelines that safely deliver validated server software to 400,000 bare-metal servers, automated patching that keeps software secure on a biweekly cadence, metrics and crash observability, and secure operational tooling for autonomous operations. We move fast to deliver for customers while maintaining operational excellence across these mission-critical services.
We are a Boston-based group building toward a future where server software tests, patches, and deploys itself: safely, securely, on schedule, with full visibility. There is significant greenfield opportunity, because CI and safe deployment for stateful bare-metal systems at global scale have almost no off-the-shelf solutions, so our teams design from first principles.

title: Software Development Manager, GTM AI Tooling, Specialist Technology Team
description:
AWS Specialist Technology Team (STT) is seeking a Software Development Manager to lead the Specialist GTM AI Tooling engineering team, the group building AI-native, agentic solutions that are fundamentally transforming how AWS Go-To-Market (GTM) teams turn customer opportunities into sales plays, and how those plays reach thousands of AWS field team members in the tools where they already work. If you want to build production agentic AI systems that impact thousands of users daily (not research prototypes, but real AI agents solving real problems), this is the role for you.
You will own and grow a team of Software Development Engineers responsible for building brand new and enhancing existing products that collectively connect AWS's go-to-market strategy to field execution:
- Specialist Knowledge Vault (SKV) - An AI-first knowledge service that uses purpose-built crawlers to index specialist content from a wide range of sources, which removes manual consolidation. SKV lets Technical Field Communities (TFCs) endorse golden content, add agent steering, build reusable playbooks, and flag outdated or incorrect content. SKV powers the AWS Specialist Agent, which more than 11,000 field team members used across nearly 100,000 conversations in its first three months.
- SKV Playbooks for GTM - Your team will own playbooks in SKV and extend them to natively represent GTM sales plays, including positioning guidance for every stage of the sales funnel, so AI agents deliver the right play to sellers with endorsed content and clear provenance. You will build the capabilities that let domain and industry leaders author with AI assistance, draft and test changes before they go live, detect duplicate or conflicting plays, and score playbook health, then migrate AWS's service-aligned GTM domains onto the platform.
- SKV Recommendations Engine - Your team will own the closed-loop AI/ML recommendation service that analyzes agent conversations, telemetry, and customer feedback signals to tell content owners what to fix next: knowledge gaps where the agent had no good answer, and inaccurate or outdated content it should no longer trust. Recommendations become next-best actions, such as updating a playbook, refreshing a first call deck, or creating new solution guidance, which agents can draft automatically for human review.
- Alchemy - The platform where AWS GTM teams capture and prioritize customer use cases and map first-party and third-party solutions to them. Alchemy's taxonomy, data products, and MCP server, which now reaches more than three times as many users as its web interface, provide the structured GTM foundation and downstream integrations that the SKV experience builds on.
This is a high-impact, AI-first leadership role where you will architect agentic systems, ship production GenAI features, and lead a team solving problems at the intersection of knowledge management, agentic authoring, multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and closed-loop measurement, all at AWS scale, using the very AI services AWS builds for its customers.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead the engineering team that owns GTM playbooks and the recommendations engine within the Specialist Knowledge Vault, along with the Alchemy platform and its integrations.
- Architect and ship production agentic AI systems using LLMs, RAG, MCP, and multi-agent orchestration, delivering endorsed sales plays, assets, and next-best actions to field teams in the tools where they already work.
- Build, manage, and develop a high-performing SDE team, maintaining Amazon's hiring bar while fostering a culture of technical ownership, rapid experimentation, and operational excellence.
- Drive the move of GTM authoring from hand-maintained sales plays to agent-assisted playbooks in KV, with versioning, pre-publish testing, conflict detection, and health scoring that give field teams confidence in AI output.
- Evolve the recommendations engine from identifying knowledge gaps and inaccurate content to recommending and drafting the next best action, using signals such as agent conversations, field adoption, pipeline, and customer feedback.
- Own the technical strategy and roadmap across all products, making trade-offs between speed-to-delivery and long-term platform scalability, in close partnership with the engineering teams that share the KV platform.
- Partner with Product, Science, GTM, TFC, and field leadership to translate ambiguous problems into engineering deliverables, and represent the team in executive reviews with Directors and VPs.
About the team
You will be joining a high-growth engineering organization that is at the forefront of applying generative AI and agentic technologies to transform how AWS GTM teams plan, author, and deliver strategy to the field. The pace of innovation is high, the problems are ambiguous, and the impact is measured by how quickly customer opportunities become sales plays in the hands of thousands of field team members and the pipeline they create. This role offers the opportunity to shape how an entire organization builds, governs, and measures AWS' go-to-market content.

title: Software Engineer II - AI/ML, Neuron Inference, Inference
description:
The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) builds the AWS Neuron SDK, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on AWS Trainium machine learning accelerators.
The Neuron Inference organization is at the forefront of optimizing inference performance for a wide range of ML models and model architectures on AWS's custom ML accelerators. We are working across the stack from PyTorch to the hardware-software boundary, our engineers build systematic infrastructure, develop high-performance kernels for ML functions, ensuring every compute unit is fine-tuned for optimal performance forour customers' demanding workloads. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the boundaries of what's
possible in AI acceleration.
As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers — from frameworks and kernels through to compiler, runtime, and collectives. We not only optimize performance on open weight models but also contribute to future architecture designs and work closely with customers to enable optimal performance on their models. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed architectures, where you'll help shape the future of AI acceleration technology.
As a Software Engineer II - AI/ML, you will design and implement business-critical features and own the performance of models on AWS Trainium end to end. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. It is a very unique learning culture. The team works closely with customers on their model enablement, providing direct support and optimization expertise to ensure their machine learning workloads achieve optimal performance on AWS ML accelerators. The team also collaborates with open source ecosystems to provide seamless integration and bring peak performance at scale for customers and developers.
This role is responsible for development, enablement, and performance tuning of a wide variety of LLM model families, including massive-scale large language models like the GLM, GPT-OSS, Kimi, and beyond. The Model Enablement team works side by side with compiler engineers and runtime engineers to create, build, and tune distributed inference solutions with AWS Trainium.
You can learn more about Neuron:
* https://awsdocs-neuron.readthedocs-hosted.com/en/latest/neuron-guide/neuron-cc/index.html
* https://aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/neuron/
* https://github.com/aws/aws-neuron-sdk
* https://www.amazon.science/how-silicon-innovation-became-the-secret-sauce-behind-awss-successAre you passionate about building software that operates at massive scale and directly impacts millions of customers? As a Software Development Engineer II at Amazon, you will design, build, and maintain systems that solve complex problems while delivering meaningful results. You will contribute across the full software development lifecycle — from working backwards from customer needs to designing, implementing, testing, deploying, and operating production software. This role offers the opportunity to tackle challenging technical problems, collaborate with talented engineers, and grow your skills while making a real impact. If you are a curious, self-motivated engineer who thrives on turning ambiguity into clarity and shipping high-quality code, we want to hear from you.
Key job responsibilities
This role contributes to building distributed inference support for PyTorch in the Neuron SDK, and tunes models to ensure the highest performance and maximize efficiency running on AWS Trainium. Strong software development in Python, system-level programming, and ML knowledge are all critical to this role. Our engineers collaborate across compiler, runtime, framework, and hardware teams to optimize machine learning workloads for our global customer base. Working at the intersection of software, hardware, and machine learning systems, you'll bring expertise in low-level optimization, system architecture, and ML model acceleration. In this role, you will:
* Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models and frameworks for deployment on custom ML hardware accelerators.
* Participate in all stages of the ML system development lifecycle, including distributed-computing-based architecture design, implementation, performance profiling, hardware-specific optimizations, testing, and production deployment.
* Build infrastructure to systematically analyze and onboard multiple models with diverse architectures.
* Understand and produce NKI (Neuron Kernel Interface) kernels, and design and implement high-performance kernels and features for ML operations, leveraging the Neuron architecture and programming models.
* Analyze and optimize system-level performance across multiple generations of Neuron hardware, using knowledge of the underlying Trainium hardware architecture to guide optimization decisions.
* Conduct detailed performance analysis using profiling tools to identify and resolve bottlenecks.
* Implement optimizations such as fusion, sharding, tiling, and scheduling.
* Conduct comprehensive testing, including unit and end-to-end model testing with continuous deployment and releases through pipelines.
* Work directly with customers to enable and optimize their ML models on AWS accelerators.
* Collaborate across teams to develop innovative optimization techniques, and share proposals, findings, and learnings with internal developers and external customers via high-quality designs and documentation.
A day in the life
You will collaborate with a cross-functional team of applied scientists, systems engineers, and product managers to deliver state-of-the-art inference capabilities for Generative AI applications. Your work will involve debugging performance issues, optimizing memory usage, and contributing to the future of Neuron's inference stack across Amazon and the Open Source Community. As you design and code solutions to help our team drive efficiencies in software architecture, you'll create metrics, implement automation and other improvements, and resolve the root cause of software defects.
You will also build high-impact solutions to deliver to our large customer base and participate in design discussions and code reviews, and communicate with internal and external stakeholders. You will work cross-functionally to help drive business decisions with your technical input. You will work in a startup-like development environment, where you're always working on the most important initiative.You will start your day reviewing operational metrics and addressing any alerts from the systems you own. From there, you might dive into designing a new feature, writing and reviewing code, or pairing with a teammate to debug a tricky issue. You will participate in design discussions, contribute to sprint planning, and document your systems so that others can learn from and extend your work. Expect regular collaboration with product and engineering partners as you shape solutions that serve customers at scale.
About the team
The Model Enablement team fosters a builder's culture where experimentation is encouraged and impact is measurable. We emphasize collaboration, technical ownership, and continuous learning. Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we're building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop their engineering expertise so they feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future. Join us to solve some of the most interesting and impactful infrastructure challenges in AI/ML today.Our team builds and operates software that powers key experiences for Amazon customers. We value technical excellence, collaboration, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Every engineer on the team has a voice in shaping our technical direction and the opportunity to mentor others. We are focused on building reliable, scalable systems while creating an inclusive environment where engineers at all levels can learn, grow, and do their best work. If you want to solve meaningful problems alongside a supportive and motivated group of engineers, this is the place for you.

- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience

title: Sr Eng, Int'l WRC Strategy, Amazon Leo, Global Regulatory Affairs
description:
Amazon Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed affordable broadband to unconnected and under-connected communities around the world.
Amaon Leo's Global Regulatory Affairs team is seeking aSr. Eng, Int'l WRC Strategy, to employ their expertise to develop and execute strategies for improving, enabling, and protecting Leo’s use of radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbits.
This is a unique opportunity to assist in the development of a global broadband satellite communication system and make a difference in bridging the digital divide.
Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum
This position is in Arlington, VA; Some travel, both domestic and international, will be required.
Key job responsibilities
The Sr Eng, Int'l WRC Strategy will develop detailed analysis products and strategies to enable Leo's use of radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbits. Functions include:
• Developing and executing technical and advocacy strategies to support Leo ITU objectives;
• Developing tools and analyses to support ITU study initiatives, international and domestic regulatory meetings, and the technical foundations for international and national satellite filings and license applications;
• Participating in ITU study groups, Regional Telecommunications Organizations, and other multilateral and regulatory bodies to advance the strategy for enabling and protecting Leo's use of radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbits;
• Analyzing information related to satellite filings, status of satellite spectrum allocations and relevant sharing studies;
• Anticipating spectrum and regulatory needs and engage with the Leo satellite and architecture design teams, licensing teams, coordination teams, and legal teams to communicate spectrum and regulatory considerations as they relate to system objectives
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to identify tradeoffs, risks, and opportunities; remove bottlenecks; and establish mechanisms to speed progress.
The ideal candidate has experience serving as a member of national delegations to ITU meetings, knowledge of the ITU Radio Regulations and domestic Satellite Regulations, knowledge of communications satellite architectures and link budgets, and experience in developing sharing studies between telecommunications services. Additionally, the candidate must have the ability to effectively communicate solutions to complex technical problems and advocate before regulatory and multilateral bodies.
A day in the life
The Sr Eng, Int'l WRC Strategy will develop analysis and simulations to model the Leo network, demonstrate compliance with international regulatory requirements, analyze and propose frameworks for spectrum and orbit use internationally, and determine sharing opportunities for co-existing with other providers of satellite services as well as with telecommunications services that use our frequency bands. You will develop, present, and defend technical studies and execute the strategy in ITU study groups, Regional Telecommunications Organizations, and other multilateral and regulatory bodies. You will work closely with the satellite and communications systems design teams and coordination teams, and business teams to ensure that the Leotechnology, business, and regulatory roadmaps are aligned.
The ideal candidate has knowledge of satellite systems and the applicable Radio Regulations, Rules of Procedure, and ITU-R Recommendations and experience conducting sharing and interference analyses.
About the team
The Global Regulatory Affairs team is responsible for enabling and protecting Amazon Leo's use of radio frequency spectrum at home and abroad, defining and leading the Amazon Leo regulatory agenda. The team operates worldwide, engaging with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and regional organizations, coordinating the use of spectrum with other operators, gaining country access, and promoting safety in space. The Global Regulatory Affairs team is also responsible for licensing and collaborates with associations, government agencies, and other satellite operators in order to advocate for rules and regulations in the best interest of our customers. This team works in close collaboration with the Leo technical design and business teams to optimize for spectrum sharing and customer experience as well as with Amazon’s public policy and legal teams to enhance the overall regulatory strategy.

- 5+ years of Space Vehicle/Satellite Operations, Space Communications or related industry experience

- Experience in the application of the ITU Radio Regulations
- Experience in developing technical studies and advancing proposals within regulatory and multilateral bodies

- Experience analyzing satellite communications systems in non-geostationary orbit
- Experience in ITU regulations related to satellite communications systems in non-geostationary orbit
- Experience developing in-house tools and products for analysis of satellite communication systems
