The Atlanta Journal-Constitution is one of the most storied brands in journalism, with a legacy that stretches back more than a century. Our mission is to be the most essential and engaging source of news for the people of Atlanta, Georgia and the South, and we have a vision to transform this great institution into a modern media company.
That’s where you come in.
We are looking for a digital-first Associate Video Producer who is excited to build their skills in writing, shooting, producing, editing and, most importantly, telling great stories.
You’ll work alongside experienced producers, journalists and creatives to develop video journalism and explainers across both vertical and horizontal formats. Your work may appear on the AJC’s owned-and-operated platforms as well as YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and other emerging platforms.

Continue developing proficiency across writing, reporting, producing, shooting and editing with the goal of taking on increasingly complex productions

The New Verticals team is building the future of local commerce through expanding our product offerings on our marketplace platform. title: Mechanical Engineer, Consumer Electronics
description:
About Us
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics.
The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.
Role Overview
We’re looking for a mechanical engineer who designs and builds connected consumer and enterprise devices, including SmartScale, lockers, POS systems, and hardware for emerging automation and robotics applications. In this role, you will help define what to build and own mechanical development from ambiguous user or business needs through architecture, rapid prototyping, and field pilots.
This is a build-heavy role on a small, senior, multidisciplinary team. You'll work directly with suppliers, supported by an NPI/program partner, and provide mechanical leadership during new product introduction (NPI). Specialist reliability expertise can support deeper validation as programs mature.
San Francisco-based candidates are preferred; hybrid arrangements are acceptable. The role includes hands-on collaboration around prototypes and lab work.
Key Responsibilities
Help define product requirements and features from customer needs and business priorities. Explain trade-offs among user experience, performance, cost, reliability, and development time.
Build prototypes for new product ideas, partner on pilot design, and turn findings from real use into requirements and designs for larger pilots. Communicate what was learned and what should happen next.
Create CAD, drawings, and physical prototypes; choose materials, components, and fabrication methods appropriate to the development stage.
Apply mechanical fundamentals, tolerance analysis, and targeted calculations or simulation to the risks that matter. Design and run physical tests to check assumptions.
Integrate mechanical designs with electronics, sensors, and firmware, and debug problems across those interfaces with teammates.
Serve as the mechanical engineering lead with manufacturing partners during NPI: investigate mechanical and build-quality issues, assess proposed changes, and help define and verify corrective actions.
Work directly with suppliers on prototype parts, design feedback, build issues, and readiness for larger pilots. Bring in specialist support for safety, reliability, tooling, or production questions as needed.
Required Qualifications
Hands-on experience taking a physical product or subsystem from incomplete requirements through mechanical design, prototyping, debugging, and testing, with evidence of learning from users or real operating conditions.
Strong mechanical design fundamentals, including materials and process selection, fit and tolerances, assembly, and practical reliability considerations.
Proficiency with a mechanical CAD package such as SolidWorks, Creo, NX, or equivalent, and the ability to create drawings and specifications suppliers can use.
Product judgment: you can question requirements, understand the customer problem, and explain technical choices in terms of cost, usability, performance, and business value.
Ability to operate independently through ambiguity, prioritize work, and communicate decisions and risks clearly.
Experience collaborating with suppliers or manufacturing partners and with engineers from other disciplines.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Must be comfortable regularly exercising discretion and independent judgment in performing job duties, including evaluating options, making informed decisions, and determining appropriate courses of action within the scope of assigned responsibilities.
Preferred Qualifications
Strongly preferred: experience bringing products into production, supporting NPI, or resolving manufacturing defects, ideally in mass production. This may include design for manufacturing and assembly, tooling, reliability testing, or field failure analysis. Personally leading a high-volume ramp is not required.
Experience in a startup, a small hardware team, or another setting where you helped define the problem and owned work across disciplinary boundaries.
Basic electrical engineering, firmware, or programming capability that helps you build and debug integrated prototypes.
Experience with electromechanical products, mechanisms, enclosures, sensors, or merchant-facing hardware.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Drive
location: San Francisco, CA; Sunnyvale, CA; Seattle, WA
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Drive powers deliveries placed through merchants' own channels—including their websites, mobile apps, and phone orders—using DoorDash's logistics network. The Drive Machine Learning team builds the prediction and intelligence systems that power this business, including delivery and pickup time estimation, merchant prep-time prediction, order release optimization, logistics decision-making, and AI-powered delivery quality signals.
Drive presents a unique machine learning challenge. Every merchant has different operational workflows, preparation patterns, and customer expectations, requiring models that generalize across millions of deliveries while adapting to highly diverse merchant behavior. Our team has significant opportunities to improve prediction accuracy, optimize logistics decisions, and build AI-native experiences that directly improve merchant, consumer, and dasher outcomes.
About the Role
As a Machine Learning Engineer on the Drive team, you'll own machine learning systems end-to-end—from feature engineering and model development to experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous iteration.
Your work will span several high-impact problem areas:
Build next-generation machine learning models for delivery ETA, pickup ETA, merchant prep-time estimation, and order release prediction that improve reliability for merchants and consumers.
Develop deep learning models that leverage large-scale spatiotemporal, marketplace, and behavioral signals to improve prediction accuracy.
Apply reinforcement learning and optimization techniques to improve logistics decision-making, assignment strategies, and marketplace efficiency.
Build AI-native product experiences using large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). For example, transform pickup photos, item verification flows, receipts, and drop-off images into structured quality signals that help verify orders, prevent delivery defects, and improve issue resolution.
Design and run rigorous online experiments, production monitoring, and model iteration to continuously improve performance.
Partner closely with software engineers, product managers, data scientists, and platform teams to bring new machine learning capabilities into production at scale.
You'll have the opportunity to work across traditional machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimization, and multimodal AI while solving some of the most challenging logistics problems at DoorDash.
You're excited about this opportunity because...
You enjoy solving large-scale machine learning problems that directly impact millions of deliveries.
You have a strong sense of ownership and enjoy taking models from research through production.
You're comfortable working in ambiguous environments where experimentation and iteration drive product decisions.
You care about both model quality and production reliability.
You're excited to work across a diverse set of ML techniques—from neural networks and optimization to multimodal AI.
You collaborate well across engineering, product, and data science teams.
We’re excited about you because…
5+ years of industry experience building and shipping production machine learning systems with measurable business impact (Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD).
Strong experience developing production machine learning models using modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and distributed data processing technologies such as Spark and Airflow.
Experience building, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining production ML systems end-to-end.
Strong software engineering skills in Python and experience with modern ML infrastructure and tooling.
Deep expertise in at least one of the following areas:
Deep Learning

description:
About the Team
Agentic Foundations, part of New Verticals ML, builds the core AI/ML intelligence that powers high-quality, scalable agents at DoorDash, and proves it through flagship agent experiences such as the Ask grocery assistant. We operate as a closed loop: new models, evals, and representations make our agents better, and real-world agent usage surfaces the gaps that drive our next foundations work.
About the Role
We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join Agentic Foundations with a primary focus on Vertical Agent Development. You will own the continuous improvement of our flagship agents, starting with the Ask Assistant, using an eval-driven loop to make them faster, more cost-efficient, and more reliable for millions of customers. You will also help us bring this approach to new agentic experiences for Merchants and Dashers, turning promising ideas into production-ready agents.
This is a chance to work at the intersection of LLMs, agents, post-training, and evals on problems that ship. You will partner closely with engineers working on agentic memory, agent-compatible product representations, and post-training of small language models (SLMs), so that what we learn from production agents feeds directly back into our foundations, and what we build there makes our agents better.
You will report into the engineering lead on our New Verticals AI/ML team. We expect this role to be hybrid with some time in-office and some time remote.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Raise the quality of our Consumer agents: build and refine our eval harness-optimization loop to pinpoint failure modes, then iterate on prompts, tools, skills, and context, and measure the impact on real customer tasks.

Launch new agents: take agentic opportunities for Merchants and Dashers from early exploration to production.
Turn foundations into product impact: work with teammates on agentic memory, agent-compatible product representations, and post-training SLMs for steerable generative recommendation, and bring those capabilities into production agents.
Shape the roadmap: partner with engineering, product, and business leaders to define an ML-driven strategy for our fast-growing grocery and retail delivery business.
We’re excited about you because you have…
3+ years of industry ML experience, including hands-on work building and shipping LLM-based agents (tool use, context management, prompting, guardrails) and improving them with evals and data
Experience with post-training or fine-tuning of open-weights models (e.g., SFT, preference optimization, or RL), ideally including small language models, and sound judgment on quality, latency, and cost trade-offs
Strong foundation in NLP and machine learning, with proficiency in Python and frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow
M.S. or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, Math, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience, plus a collaborative, growth-minded approach and a drive for measurable impact

location: San Francisco, CA; Sunnyvale, CA; Seattle, WA; New York City, NY
description:
About the Team
The Spark Platform team owns and operates DoorDash's Apache Spark ecosystem — the execution runtime, remote shuffle service, cluster scheduler, and reliability tooling that powers the company's data, analytics, and ML workloads. We run Spark across the company at significant scale and continue to expand the workloads, capabilities, and consumer base we serve. Orchestrating and operating thousands of Spark cluster deployments is a complex distributed system problem which the team invests heavily in runtime optimization, systems architecture, multi-tenant scheduling, and end-user tooling.
About the Role
As a Senior Software Engineer on Spark Platform, you will set the technical direction for our in-house Spark deployment and shape the architecture that will run DoorDash's data, analytics, and ML compute for the next five years and beyond. You will own the deep, cross-cutting problems that span the runtime, the shuffle service, the scheduler, and the overall service reliability — making the architectural calls that compound across the platform's lifetime. You will partner with the Engineering Manager on technical roadmap, hiring, and team shape, and act as the senior technical voice in cross-team partnerships with Data Engineering, ML Platform, and product engineering teams that depend on the platform.
You must be located in San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Seattle, or New York City for this hybrid position. You will report into the Engineering Manager on our Spark Platform team.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Set the multi-year technical direction for an in-house Spark-on-Kubernetes platform — runtime, shuffle, scheduler, reliability — and make the architectural calls that compound for years.
Own the deepest distributed-systems problems on the team: shuffle architecture, multi-tenant scheduling, runtime performance, and the failure modes that only show up at scale.
Partner with the Engineering Manager on technical roadmap, hiring, interview design, and team shape as the team continues to grow.
Uplevel the rest of the team through design reviews, mentorship, and raising the bar on what we ship.
Represent Spark Platform in cross-team architecture forums and shape how data, analytics, and ML workloads land on the platform.
We're excited about you because…
B.S., M.S., or PhD in Computer Science or equivalent.
6+ years of industry experience designing and operating distributed systems at scale.
Deep, hands-on experience with Apache Spark — internals, query execution, shuffle, the executor/driver model — at platform scale on Amazon EMR, Databricks, or an in-house deployment, with a focus on platform operations (runtime upgrades, cluster lifecycle, shuffle, observability, multi-tenant scheduling) rather than authoring individual Spark jobs.
Production experience with one or more of: remote/external shuffle systems (Celeborn, Magnet, Cosco, or similar), batch/big-data schedulers (YuniKorn, Volcano, Kueue, or the Spark-on-Kubernetes operator), or the observability and SRE patterns that make distributed compute platforms operable.

DoorDash's MDX team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared foundation that ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo rely on to build and run ML-powered products. We work across the full ML lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, serving, and monitoring. Our mission is to increase the velocity and reliability of ML-driven business impact across the company. A central pillar of that work is agentic infrastructure. We are building systems that let agents accelerate and operate the ML workflow itself, including auto research, where agents explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and self-healing systems that detect, diagnose, and remediate failures in ML pipelines and production models with minimal human intervention.
About the Role
You will join a small, high-leverage team building the agentic layer of DoorDash's ML infrastructure. You'll design and build the systems that let agents accelerate how ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo develop, ship, and operate models. That includes auto research systems that explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and agentic developer support that helps ML engineers move through training, evaluation, deployment, and debugging faster. You'll own well-scoped components end to end, from design through production, working across agent orchestration, tooling and integrations with our ML platform, evaluation of agent behavior, and observability. This role is ideal for an engineer with a strong backend foundation who is excited to apply AI agents to real engineering workflows, learns quickly, and wants to grow into technical leadership in a fast-moving area where model capabilities, tooling, and best practices change month to month.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build agentic systems that increase the velocity of ML development across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, helping ML engineers get from idea to production model faster.
Design and implement infrastructure that lets agents propose, run, and evaluate modeling experiments.
Build agentic developer support for the ML lifecycle, such as agents that help engineers set up training jobs, debug failing pipelines, review model deployments, and navigate our platform.
Develop evaluation and observability for agent behavior, so we can measure whether agents are actually helping, catch regressions early, and build the trust needed to give them more autonomy.
Work with production standards in mind, including reliability, safety guardrails, cost controls, monitoring, and clear playbooks, so that agentic workflows can run against real ML systems.
Partner closely with ML engineers, data scientists, and platform teams to understand where their time goes and turn those workflows into durable, reusable platform capabilities.
Grow quickly in a fast-moving area, with the chance to shape how agents are used to build and operate ML systems at a company of this scale.
We're excited about you because…

title: Staff Security Engineer, Security Enablement
description:
About the Role
Global Safety and Security (GSS) protects our people, our sites, and the physical and logical systems that keep the business running. Our security and protection programs are never single-team efforts: one rollout can touch physical security operations, customer experiences, site readiness, hardware provisioning, networking, cloud infrastructure, identity, and the data platforms above them — spanning many countries, on timelines tied to leases, permits, and vendors.
About the Team
We are hiring a Staff Security Engineer to help design and deliver strategic and durable security services. You own the technical and architectural plan, strategic partner engagement with technology providers, the delivery sequence, the dependencies, and the program status leadership relies on. You are accountable for outcomes influencing teams that you don’t manage. You will collaborate with software engineers, third-party providers, physical security operations, project managers running site readiness and provisioning, and networking and cloud infrastructure partners, and you will keep managers, directors, and senior leaders informed.
Security Enablement Engineering delivers security paved paths and capabilities that address systemic security issues through well-designed customer experiences, easy-to-adopt and robust, well-architected security solutions, systematically reducing organizational risk.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own the design of our physical security systems integration layer — such as access control (PACS) and video management (VMS) platforms, the APIs they expose, and the connectors that carry their data into our systems of record.
Own end-to-end design and delivery of multi-domain security services spanning physical security systems, hardware provisioning and site readiness, cloud and network infrastructure, identity and access management, key management, and the reporting/observability layers on top. You’ll bring expertise deploying security solutions at scale across many of these domains.
Partner with our software engineers from design through implementation, ensuring the right security outcomes are achieved. Propose and review architecture, design highly resilient, secure and scalable solutions, deliver proactive feedback to drive continuous improvement, hold the interface contracts, and support services in production ensuring operational excellence.
Own the cloud footprint of the security stack. The AWS services that host and scale these systems, the identity and network boundaries around them.
Own execution of complex and ambiguous security initiatives through detailed working-backwards plans. Start from the outcome and the date, then derive the dependency chain, critical path, owners, and the decisions that must land before each gate.
Look around corners. Surface and manage delivery risks before they escalate. Keep a risk register that’s well managed with an owner, a mitigation, and a delivery date.
Unblock, and escalate when unblocking requires it. Resolve most cross-team friction through direct collaboration. Escalate early, with a recommendation, and tradeoffs to leadership. Escalation is a deliberate tool, not a last resort.
Be the single source of truth on status. Concise written updates for senior leaders: what is on track, what is at risk, what changed, what decision we need. Manage stakeholder expectations from leadership to individual teams, apply strong problem solving and negotiation skills, and earn the trust of partners and teams.
Drive technical decisions to closure and operate through ambiguity. Frame the trade-offs, make recommendations on tooling (build/buy) and document what was decided and why.
Contribute to the vision, strategy, technical direction, and success metrics. Mentor engineers and program managers across GSS and partner teams. Review their plans, coach them on written status and risk framing, and help continually raise the operational and security bar. Develop shared goals with security partners, and identify solutions that optimize or automate manual, inefficient processes.
We’re excited about you because…
You have led multi-team, multi-quarter technical programs and owned the outcome across organizational boundaries.
You have a deep understanding of at least three security engineering domains and broad understanding across many: Identity and Access Management, Physical Security Systems, Security Operations, Detection and Response, DevSecOps, Security Architecture and Engineering, and Network Security.
You can read a network diagram, reason about a cloud deployment topology, understand hardware and firmware lifecycles, and hold a credible conversation with an infrastructure engineer about their constraints.
Global-scale software or cloud rollouts, including vendor-supplied platforms deployed across many sites and regions, with the integration and migration work that implies.
Exceptional written and verbal communication — plans and status a director can act on and a senior engineer will not dismiss, and the range to convey security priorities and concepts to experts and non-experts alike.
Influence without authority, agility in re-planning when reality changes rather than defending the original plan, and comfort with physical-world constraints: sites, hardware, permits, and installers do not behave like pure software programs.
You have raised the bar for others without managing them — mentoring engineers and program managers, and improving plans and status through proactive feedback.
You have strong ownership, urgency, autonomy and drive. You are willing to roll up your sleeves and dive into the details to understand and drive your programs, and you focus on progress, not perfection.
Qualifications
Required
6+ years in security or infrastructure engineering, including 4+ leading multi-team technical programs.
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Security Engineering, Information Systems, or equivalent years of experience in a related technical field
Expertise with cloud-based services and infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud, etc.)
Hands-on depth with enterprise access control and video platforms (Lenel, Genetec, Milestone, or peers) and the APIs and integrations around them.
Project planning and execution skills that include JIRA experience, reviewing technical design documents, security controls, estimating, and scheduling.
Preferred
Physical security, access control, or safety-technology programs; a security or trust-and-safety organization; standing up program practice where none existed.
Proficiency in SQL data analysis, Python coding, and other automation tooling.
Experience with building Agentic workflows.

title: Robotics Field Service Technician
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
The Fleet Operations Team drives uptime and operational performance across Formic’s growing fleet of deployed robotic systems. Working inside live manufacturing environments, the team diagnoses issues, restores production, and continuously improves system reliability at scale. Fleet Operations operates at the intersection of robotics, controls, and real-world factory execution, ensuring Formic’s automation delivers consistent, measurable performance across diverse industrial applications.
About the role:
As a Robotics Field Service Technician, you are a hands-on member of Formic’s Fleet Operations team. Working closely with Engineering and senior field staff, you will execute preventive maintenance, carry out directed corrective repairs, and represent Formic directly within customer facilities.
This is a hands-on, safety-focused role in uptime-critical environments. Success requires disciplined execution of established procedures, calm work during production interruptions, and clear documentation. Your work directly supports fleet performance, customer satisfaction, and long-term system reliability.
In this role you will:
Execute scheduled preventive maintenance on robotic manufacturing cells following established checklists and procedures
Perform directed corrective maintenance and repairs as assigned by engineering, dispatch, or senior technicians
Respond to on-site service calls, follow structured troubleshooting steps, and escalate complex or unresolved issues to engineering
Provide hands-on technical support to customer operators and maintenance teams
Log service activity, asset updates, and spare part requirements in CMMS systems
Follow assigned field schedules and coordinate day-to-day logistics with customers and internal stakeholders
Monitor system performance using Formic dashboards and fleet tools, and report anomalies to engineering
Document service work and follow-up actions with clarity and precision
Flag recurring issues or failure patterns to engineering for further investigation
Build professional, trusted relationships with plant managers and site personnel
Operate with strict adherence to safety standards, including LOTO and industrial compliance
Support RCA sessions, audits, and continuous improvement initiatives as directed
Continuously build technical skills across robotics, controls, networking, and industrial systems
What makes you a great fit:
2+ years of hands-on field service or maintenance experience supporting robotic or industrial automation systems
Solid troubleshooting skills across electrical, mechanical, PLC, or robotic control systems
Ability to read electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and pneumatic drawings
Experience using CMMS platforms to track and report maintenance activity
Comfortable with local travel up to 80% and overnight travel up to 50%
Clear written and verbal communicator capable of producing structured service documentation
Demonstrated commitment to safety and disciplined, checklist-driven field execution
Ability to follow detailed work instructions and reliably complete directed tasks with minimal oversight
Bonus points if you have:
Experience working hands-on with 6-axis robot brands such as Fanuc, KUKA, Yaskawa, ABB, or Universal Robots (e.g. maintenance, troubleshooting, basic programming)
Familiarity with palletizing, case packing, pick-and-place, or conveyor systems
Experience in food, beverage, packaging, CPG, or other high-speed manufacturing environments
Prior customer-facing field experience
Spanish language proficiency
Our Total Rewards:
At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
Paid Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it. 15 days of paid time off, in addition to company holidays
Compensation Philosophy
Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.
This role is paid hourly with a posted range of $25–$32  per hour. Based on the nature of field service work - which consistently runs approximately 50+ hours per week including travel, site activity, and documentation - total annualized earnings typically range from $71,500 - $91,520 , depending on experience, hourly rate, and actual hours worked. Overtime is paid in accordance with applicable federal and state law for all hours worked over 40 in a workweek.
Hourly Rate: $25 — $32 USD What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to  careers@formic.co .
AI Use:
At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked  here .

title: Operator I
description:
The Operator 1 position is integral to the production process at our WPC Extrusion Plant, Fiberon in Meridian, ID for composite decking manufacturing.
Starting at $20.00 / hour~
As part of the team you'll be performing, learning, and observing a variety of tasks to ensure quality control, efficient operations, and a clean, safe working environment. Responsibilities are categorized into "See," "Learn," "Do," and "Teach" as per our training and task prioritization framework.
NOW HIRING for All Shift
Shift A Sunday - Tuesday + every other Saturday for 12 hour shifts
Shift B Nights! Sunday - Tuesday + every other Saturday for 12 hour shifts (Pay differential of +$1/hr)
Shift C Wednesday - Friday + every other Saturday for 12 hour shifts
Shift D Nights! Wednesday - Friday + every other Saturday for 12 hour shifts (Pay differential of +$1/hr)
Let us know what Shift is best for you
Key Responsibilities:
Core Duties (DO)
•    Conduct color and defect inspections on boards.
•    Perform board measurements and align boards on carts.
•    Pull and band scrap boards, and prepare scrap bundles.
•    Prep carts for finished goods bundles, attach end tags, and package completed finished goods.
•    Label products accurately and ensure proper storage of tools after cleaning.
•    Operate banders, staple guns, and pull carts.
•    Refill banding roll carts and cut black slip sheeting.
•    Move completed, tagged units to designated locations (MCP).
•    Clear production line jam-ups and assist others in packaging and wrapping units.
•    Communicate defects and issues with operators, leads, and supervisors.
•    Inspect groove and side printing for accuracy.
•    Assist with First Piece Inspection (FPI) and line clearance.
•    Monitor raw material supplies and restock as necessary.
•    Isolate and identify defective products per established procedures.
•    Dust walls and equipment, and clean as per the instruction schedule.
•    Perform heavy cleaning tasks, such as truck dumps, and empty trash.
•    Weigh and manage wood bins before disposal.
•    Update Tier 1 boards and maintain accurate records (e.g., FPI, BOM, changeover forms).
Learning and Growth Tasks (LEARN)
•    Learn to string up extrusion lines.
•    Understand the operation of serialized labeling systems.
•    Assist with cooling water removal processes.
•    Monitor SPC screens to ensure production quality standards.
Observational Tasks (SEE)
•    Observe printing and adherence of completed product tags.
•    Ensure tagging and packaging meet required standards.
•    Witness updates and maintenance of production paperwork.
Qualifications and Skills:
•    Previous experience in a manufacturing or production setting is preferred but not required.
•    Basic mechanical aptitude and an eye for detail.
•    Ability to communicate effectively and collaborate with team members.
•    Must be comfortable with physical labor, including lifting, bending, and standing for extended periods.
Physical Requirements
•    Strength & Endurance:
o    Lift and move boards, bundles, and raw materials weighing up to [insert specific weight, e.g., 50 lbs].

ITW Contamination Control , a division of ITW, a Fortune 250 global industrial leader , is seeking a dynamic and technical Product Manager to join our Marketing team. As our Product Manager, you will own the full product line lifecycle across the Chemtronics and Techspray portfolios. You will act as the bridge between market needs and technical reality, ensuring our solutions maintain a clear and strong value proposition.

Revenue & margin growth: Measurable Year over year growth in assigned product lines, tracked against unit volume, revenue, and gross margin targets, driven by sharp product positioning, pricing, and portfolio decisions.
New product introduction (NPI) velocity: Consistent delivery of new products, on schedule, with clear competitive differentiation, by owning the front end (customer requirements and business case, beta trial coordination and feedback) and launch readiness.
Market share capture: Support sales team with the competitive analysis, positioning, and tools they need to win share in core electronics, aerospace, medical device and industrial cleaning segments.
Voice-of-customer translation: Partner with sales and other functions to conduct VOC for new product development.
Cross-functional leadership: Seen by Lab, Operations, Sales, and Marketing as a collaborative partner who builds alignment and makes clear, well-informed product strategy decisions.

Strategic Innovation: Partner with Lab, Operations, Sales, and Marketing to develop and execute a robust Innovation Roadmap; own product strategy and roadmap for assigned cleaning chemistries across both the Chemtronics and Techspray brands (e.g., defluxers, vapor-degreasing fluids, heat transfer fluids, maintenance cleaners); lead products through each phase process to ensure competitive differentiation and timely market entry.
Go-to-Market Excellence: Develop and implement comprehensive go-to-market plans, including pricing strategies and sales policies designed to achieve revenue and margin targets.
Market Intelligence & VOC: Coordinate Voice of the Customer (VOC) exercises to define regional and global requirements for new product launches.
Technical & Channel Partnership: The Product Manager develops enough technical expertise to accurately interpret customer challenges, translate them into actionable technical requirements, and then communicate solutions back to commercial audiences.
Business Intelligence: Perform deep market research and competitive analysis; utilize data-driven analysis to track unit volumes, revenue, and margins to inform future product direction.
Regulatory Leadership: Understand how our products fit within industry standards and regulations, including Aviation (Boeing, Airbus), Electronics (IPC, J-STD), ESD/static-control standards (ANSI/ESD S20.20), and environmental regulations such as REACH, RoHS, VOCs, PFAS, and TSCA, and partner with Lab to ensure compliance informs roadmap and positioning decisions.

Data Proficiency: A strong preference for data-driven decision-makers; experience with Power BI, HubSpot CRM, and ERP systems.
Commercial Savvy: A passion for technology and innovation with a proven, quantifiable track record of launching products and analyzing segmented P&L statements to impact the financial success of a product line.
Leadership Instincts: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a collaborative leadership style and the ability to manage multiple priorities independently in a fast-paced environment.

You will join a dynamic and diverse team in a professional office setting. This role requires the ability to travel up to 15–20% domestically, ranging from day trips to week-long excursions depending on the product lifecycle.

At ITW, we offer a professional environment where your decisions directly affect the financial success of the product line. High school diploma or GED plus 1–2 years of experience in a related field
Ability to work safely with mechanical and electrical equipment; familiarity with safely moving tools & equipment
Basic knowledge of welding, hydraulics, and/or electrical systems
Basic understanding of mechanical troubleshooting
Basic knowledge of CO₂ and Freon systems, plumbing, and soldering
Strong customer service skills, including resolving customer concerns
Ability to manage expense reports and travel-related documentation
Willingness to grow into a Service/Repair Technician role
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record

The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this Job, the employee may:
Lift up to 75 lbs. with or without assistance, kneel, squat, bend, push/pull
Climb up to 10 ft with an A-frame ladder; occasional roof access may be necessary through extension or fixed ladders greater than 20 feet
Extensive walking, 3-5 miles/day; extensive driving, 5-6 hours/day
Move into different positions to accomplish tasks in many environments, including tight and confined spaces
Operate motor vehicles or heavy equipment (i.e., forklift), machinery, and power tools.
Working Conditions
Office facility and customer facilities (including commercial kitchens of various types of businesses)
Exposure to noise, heat, cold, slippery, wet, dirty conditions may occur

Normal business hours with occasional/frequent/extended hours as needed (may include nights/weekends)

Installation Technician II
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. ITW FEG has the largest service network in this industry to support our global customers, with highly specialized technicians and best-in-class supply chain procedures. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
The Installation Technician II is responsible for leading and/or supporting with the installation, assembly, inspection, and basic maintenance of commercial food equipment. This role supports installation projects by uncrating, moving, positioning, and assembling equipment, as well as ensuring proper operation under supervision. The Installation Technician will also be responsible for driving service and delivery vehicles to transport equipment safely to job sites using lift-gates.

title: Inventory Control Coordinator
description:
Job Description:
Why this Role Matters
The Inventory Control Coordinator at ITW in Paris, Kentucky plays a critical role in ensuring manufacturing operations have the tooling, materials, and non-inventory supplies needed to meet customer demand. You will leverage analytical thinking and 80/20 principles to optimize inventory levels, improve material availability, reduce stock-outs and excess inventory, and strengthen supplier performance. Success in this role means maintaining a reliable supply chain that supports operational efficiency, cost control, and continuous improvement.
What You Will Do
Analyze inventory levels and consumption patterns to ensure on-hand materials meet manufacturing requirements, including expedited and exceptional production needs as communicated.
Support root cause analysis initiatives by evaluating reports, identifying usage trends, monitoring consumption changes, and investigating unusual inventory patterns.
Manage the RFQ process for all non-inventory materials, tooling, and related supplies.
Place purchase orders and proactively follow up on open orders while ensuring compliance with established pricing, discounts, and purchasing terms.
Establish and maintain Kanban systems and visual min-max inventory controls to promote effective communication, reorder accuracy, and operational continuity during employee absences.
Purchase replacement tooling and machine components in accordance with established Kanban replenishment processes.
Prepare, assemble, and issue tooling kits to support efficient manufacturing machine setups.
Maintain inventory and purchasing systems to effectively communicate inventory status, usage, orders, pricing, delivery schedules, and deadlines with internal stakeholders and suppliers.
Procure materials and services from approved suppliers, communicate price changes, and expedite deliveries to support operational requirements.
Collaborate with suppliers to develop and maintain replenishment, restocking, and consignment inventory programs.
Negotiate credits, pricing adjustments, and delivery accommodations; communicate production schedule changes and secure supplier commitments to prevent shipment delays while processing purchase orders.
Maintain accurate purchasing documentation, including acknowledgments, amendments, and supply requisitions; review packing slips for accuracy, resolve discrepancies, and submit documentation to Accounts Payable to ensure timely supplier payments.
Assist with supplier scorecards and performance evaluations while supporting supplier consolidation, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Partner with Accounts Payable to investigate and resolve discrepancies involving packing slips, purchase orders, and supplier invoices.
Generate and analyze monthly spending reports, providing leadership with insights into purchasing trends and cost management opportunities.
Manage inventory levels and place orders for production and packaging supplies through the SAP system to ensure uninterrupted operations.
Develop and maintain min-max inventory strategies for production and packaging supplies to optimize stock levels and material availability.
Conduct routine cost analyses and sourcing reviews to identify savings opportunities, improve supplier performance, and support cost-effective purchasing decisions.
Additional duties as assigned.
What You Bring (Requirements)
High School Diploma or GED required; Bachelor’s degree preferred.
3+ years of purchasing, inventory control, buyer, MRO, or tooling analyst experience in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
Strong understanding of purchasing processes, inventory management, and supply chain principles.
Proficiency with SAP or similar ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications; CMMS experience (FIIX preferred).
Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and multitasking skills.
Ability to build effective relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders; maintenance parts knowledge preferred.
What’s In It for You
Join a collaborative manufacturing environment where your work directly impacts production performance and operational excellence. You will have opportunities to drive process improvements, influence inventory strategy, and partner with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Grounded in four data-driven Core Commitments, we aim to ensure all colleagues—regardless of segment, division, geography or title—experience what differentiates ITW as a great employer.

The Standard Products Engineer is responsible for supporting a high standard of performance, quality, and efficiency for current products through design and analysis of components using various engineering methods, testing and inspection. title: Videographer & Motion Editor
description:
Job Description:
Job Summary
This is a high-impact, technical role for a video and motion professional who takes pride in the craft of visual storytelling. You will be a driving force for ITW Welding's family of brands, primarily Miller and Hobart, turning brand strategies and creative briefs into authentic, genuine video content that honors our nearly 100-year legacy. You will bridge the gap between the gritty reality of the shop floor and the high-stakes precision of the corporate boardroom. You will be responsible for capturing our distinct brand voices with the same honesty found in the work itself, creating content that speaks with equal authority to the welding fabricator at the bench, the leaders in the boardroom, and the distribution partners who rely on our brand reputation to drive their sales. You are a "master of the craft" and hands-on creative partner who advises and influences the vision while executing the work with technical precision.
Responsibilities
Cinematic Execution & Technical Strategy
Serve as a primary cinematographer on set, managing composition, lighting, and sound while providing technical video expertise alongside our product experts to capture the authentic reality of the work.
Utilize our dedicated on-site studio, featuring integrated lighting solutions and professional-grade infrastructure, to execute high-polish studio shoots.
Act as a creative partner to internal marketing teams and external agencies to help define and refine the look and feel of our brands.
Audit and maintain our internal equipment identifying the glass, bodies, and lighting needed to meet the cinematic standards of a world-class brand.
Navigate complex industrial environments: utilizing professional lighting techniques to manage high-heat, high-scale manufacturing spaces with precision.
Translate strategic briefs into visual frameworks that keep our motion output steadfast, premium, and scalable.
End-to-End Production
Own the process from the first frame to the final export, moving seamlessly from high-heat industrial environments to the edit suite.
Execute expert-level color grading, pacing, and sound design to ensure every narrative is clear and every delivery is professional.
Balance "A-List" flagship productions with the development of high-quality templates for efficient, quick-turn projects.
Build and maintain a highly organized post-production system: ensuring technical consistency, file management (DAM), and scalable delivery workflows.
Collaborative Partnership
·You must be as comfortable managing a solo shoot as you are collaborating on a two-camera set or dividing post-production tasks.
·Act as a collaborative peer to our existing motion team members, providing mutual creative "pressure-testing" to ensure every frame meets the Miller standard.
·You must be comfortable working in the heat and sparks to catch the authentic moments that cannot be faked.
·Provide technical expertise and creative feedback to partner divisions, ensuring all work, internal or agency-led, lives up to our brand promises.
Qualifications
5+ years of experience in high-end video production and editing within an agency or in-house environment.
In-depth knowledge of the end-to-end video workflow, from storyboarding to pre-production lighting and final delivery.
Mastery of camera systems and professional lighting for industrial spaces.
Advanced proficiency in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and After Effects.
A formal degree in Film, Cinematography, Visual Communications, or a related field is preferred, but not required with a proven track record of impactful work.
Foundational knowledge of the welding process or prior experience shooting in industrial/manufacturing environments is a significant plus, but not a requirement.
A portfolio of work must be provided that showcases a versatile range of motion projects from social-first content to cinematic brand storytelling and national spots.
Location and Travel
This role is based at our headquarters in Appleton, Wisconsin, working out of our dedicated production studio.
Expect 20-30% travel for on-location production as project needs dictate.
Candidates must be able to move 25 lbs of gear and work safely around heavy machinery and industrial environments.

Experience with requirements gathering, documentation, and business-to-technical translation.

Experience working in offshore delivery models with structured SDLC or agile processes.
Knowledge of data governance and data quality practices.

description:
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery, we strive to foster an inclusive and diverse team, committed to making a difference. For more than 25 years, we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world to help solve some of healthcare's hardest challenges and advance what is possible.
Intuitive has been built by the efforts of great people from diverse backgrounds. We believe great ideas can come from anywhere. We strive to foster an inclusive culture built around diversity of thought and mutual respect. We lead with inclusion and empower our team members to do their best work as their most authentic selves.
Passionate people who want to make a difference drive our culture. Our team members are grounded in integrity, have a strong capacity to learn, the energy to get things done, and bring diverse, real world experiences to help us think in new ways. We actively invest in our team members to support their long-term growth so they can continue to advance our mission and achieve their highest potential.
Join a team committed to taking big leaps forward for a global community of healthcare professionals and their patients. Together, let's advance the world of minimally invasive care.
As an Embedded Software Engineer in the Future Forward organization, you will work at the forefront of innovation, rapid prototyping, and new product development. You’ll collaborate with talented cross-functional teams—including engineers, clinicians, and product managers—to advance Intuitive’s robotic surgical platform, driving the entire product lifecycle from concept to launch.
In this role, you will design, develop, and integrate embedded and platform software across a complex robotic system, interfacing with hardware, firmware, control algorithms, vision pipelines, user interfaces, and test infrastructure, including fault-injection and diagnostic frameworks. You will contribute to the architecture, implementation, and system-level integration of advanced functionalities into complete surgical robotic platforms, supporting product release and validated human use. Your work will be critical to meeting delivery milestones while ensuring safe, reliable, and compliant operation for patients worldwide.
Success in this role requires excelling in an agile, small-team environment—transforming initial concepts into robust prototypes, methodically iterating designs, and consistently maintaining exceptional product quality with a patient-first mindset.
Essential Job Duties
Design and develop robust embedded software to enable system infrastructure, including OS drivers, hardware interfaces, real-time data pipelines, inter-processor communication, error handling, and user/test applications.
Collaborate cross-functionally throughout the product lifecycle with key stakeholders to address clinical needs and safety requirements.
Translate early requirements into prototype implementations to evaluate, iterate, and advance novel robotic systems.
Conduct rigorous unit testing to support system integration and ensure reliable, robust system operation.
Contribute to hazard and failure mode analysis, defining appropriate mitigations.
Refine and iterate designs, balancing technical requirements, feasibility, schedules, and resource constraints.
Produce clear and compliant supporting documentation in alignment with Intuitive's development and quality guidelines.
Ensure all designs meet rigorous quality and safety standards per the Intuitive Quality Management System.
A minimum of 5 years of experience in developing and supporting embedded systems; or 3 years with a Master’s degree; or 1 year with a PhD.
Highly proficient in developing C/C++ embedded and real-time software for multi-core, multi-processor systems, especially on embedded Linux and QNX.
Demonstrated experience with board bring-up, device driver development, and integration of new hardware components.
Skilled in version control systems and collaborative development environments, supporting efficient, iterative improvement.
Familiarity with a wide range of communication protocols—including TCP/IP, CAN, I2C, SPI—and serialization standards such as protobuf.
Strong problem-solving skills and debugging capabilities for complex embedded software and electromechanical systems.
In-depth understanding of failure mode and risk analysis, with a track record in safety-critical, product-focused designs.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective interaction across all organizational levels.
Demonstrates passion for innovation, continuous learning, and developing solutions that make a meaningful difference in patients’ lives.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with robotics and embedded software for complex electro-mechanical systems.
Knowledgeable in Python or Matlab for automation, diagnostics, and testing.
Familiarity with FPGA development and interfaces.
Familiarity with CUDA programming and memory management concepts.
Cyber-security concepts such as secure boot, authentication and encryption.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for mission critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.

Design and build scalable, distributed Data as a Service that ingest, process, and serve data from robotics, manufacturing, engineering, and clinical sources in real time and batch modes.

Partner with engineering, analytics, and business stakeholders to evolve data contracts and models that support emerging use cases and ensure semantic consistency.

Championing a self-service data culture by building discoverable, well-documented data products and guiding teams toward empowered, autonomous data access.

Coordinate collection and preparation of financial and operations reports

Job Purpose
To ensure we are supplying customers with the highest quality products while adhering to all food and safety standards. This is accomplished by batching food product/condiments to corporate/customer approved recipes.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
• Obtains instruction from lead processor or supervisor.
• Ability to follow complete production schedules with minimal scrap/spoilage
• Keep up with volume of work required
• Visually inspects equipment at station for cleanliness or obvious maintenance problems.
• Cleans small machine components, as needed.
• Reports any problems to lead processor or supervisor.
• Makes piping connections as needed for particular process on schedule.
• Monitors equipment controls, temperature meters, valves and adjusts as needed.
• Operates forklift/pallet jack to obtain ingredients or move pallets/totes in and around processing area.
• While slow, assists processing assistants in cleaning processing areas by scrubbing walls, hosing floor, sweeping floor/emptying trash and performing other cleaning duties.
• Utilizes can openers, knives, band cutters, snips, pliers and other small items to open ingredient cases/packages.
• Maintains neat work area. Wipes spills that have occurred during mixing process.
• Records data pertaining to work completed, ingredients used, lot codes and other processing information.
• Assists in cleaning equipment and lines between recipes.
• Very occasionally obtains ingredients/supplies from warehouse.
• Obtains samples of batches and taste test.
• Asks lead, supervisor or material handler if there is any rework.
• Uses rework if there is any consistently.
• Determines ingredients required for formula/recipe and the required amount.
• Ability to safely lift 50lbs on a regular basis.
• Obtains ingredients from storage area or around work area and pours into kettle.
• Meters in other ingredients as required by watching meters and turning on/off kettle.
• Utilizes drum lift by strapping drum into lift and operating hydraulic lift with chain.
• Manually pushes drum lift to kettle and dumps drum of ingredients as needed.
• Operates controls to activate mixers and equipment.
• Monitors controls, equipment temperature, valves, and adjusts equipment to meet formula requirements.
• Hoses spills off floor and hoses towards drains.
• Obtains, measures and weighs additional ingredients to set aside in preparation for next batch or recipe.
• Assists other processors in pouring ingredients into kettles as needed.
• Collects samples and tests for pH, acidity, viscosity and solids.
• Reads test results and adjusts equipment/recipe accordingly.
• Notifies lead processor of any major adjustments needed, or problems with process.
• Transfers finished products to drum, tote, or tank by pumping through piping system.
• Operates switches to control pumps when batch is complete.
• Assists in preparing drums, totes, or tanks for storage of product by ensuring that the proper placarding information is on the package.
• Determines appropriate size of batch needed to accommodate orders and line.
• Closely monitors batch temperature while processing and waiting for packaging to ensure that product will not set prematurely.
• Operates equipment in a safe manner following GMP guidelines and keeps work area clean.
• Supports the Jacksonville plant FSQ and QRMP initiatives on any and all procedures/programs pertaining to product safety.
• Participates in meetings and have scheduling flexibility.
• Trains others as necessary.
• Fills in for other positions as necessary.
• Occasionally testing batches in the lab and recording information on proper documentation.
• Additional responsibilities of this position include assisting in the creation of a culture of safety and health by performing work safely in accordance with all company safety procedures.
• Operates equipment safely and reports any unsafe work conditions or practice to supervisor. Occupational safety and health performance is measured in this position
• Other duties as assigned

Mechanics are encouraged to wear tool pouches on their waist while working (approximately 15 pounds). Mechanics must climb on, over, under or through equipment, catwalks, railings, utility runs, small access doors, etc. Mechanics work in tight spaces under or between equipment, in crawl spaces above the ceiling and inside “confined spaces”. While in these areas, they must lift, lower or support equipment, as well as exert significant force on hand tools. title: Sr. Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience
location: Chicago/Aon Center, Illinois, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose
The Senior Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience leads the North America Procurement risk management and resilience strategy and owns responsible sourcing compliance for the region. This role owns the frameworks, governance, tools and cross-functional routines used to identify, assess, prioritize, monitor and mitigate supplier, material, financial, operational, regulatory, geopolitical, quality and sustainability-related risks, while driving supplier compliance with applicable SEDEX requirements.
The position partners closely with Category Procurement, Business Units, Supply Chain, Operations, R&D, Finance, Legal, Food Safety & Quality and Sustainability teams to embed risk into category strategies, sourcing decisions and supplier relationship management. The role strengthens supply continuity, improves decision quality and supports uninterrupted delivery of the company strategic and growth objectives.
Job Description
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
1. Risk & Resilience Strategy and Operating Model
Own and annually refresh the North America Procurement Risk & Resilience roadmap and three-year strategic plan, aligned with business priorities and ambitious risk-reduction targets.
Define the procurement risk operating model, including risk appetite, governance routines, intake and prioritization, KPI tracking and leadership escalation pathways.
Build capability roadmaps covering future-state tools, process improvements, automation opportunities and data enhancements.
Continuously improve risk frameworks, methodologies and controls based on business needs, emerging threats and lessons learned.
2. Material, Supplier and Supply Continuity Risk
Own the Material Risk Assessment methodology and annual AROP cycle, including methodology refresh, category engagement, risk scoring, mitigation planning and progress tracking.
Identify and refine the variables used to measure risk so that the highest-priority materials, suppliers and exposures are targeted for mitigation.
Lead third-party risk management across strategic and critical suppliers, monitoring financial, operational, quality, regulatory, ESG, geographic and geopolitical risks.
Partner with category teams to develop and advance mitigation plans, including alternate sourcing, dual sourcing, contingency planning and other resilience solutions.
Develop procurement resilience playbooks, conduct scenario planning and disruption simulations, and support crisis response and business recovery during supply disruptions.
Maintain accurate material risk trackers and optimize their usability, data quality and relevance for decision-making and reporting.
3. Responsible sourcing
Own North America Procurement’s SEDEX compliance program, governance and annual priorities, aligned with global requirements and business needs.
Manage supplier registration, site association and required information in SEDEX, partnering with category teams and suppliers to address gaps and maintain accurate records.
Monitor supplier and site compliance, track completion against established requirements and follow up on overdue or incomplete actions.
Coordinate with Sustainability, category teams and suppliers on SEDEX related issues, escalations and remediation actions.
Maintain SEDEX compliance dashboards and reporting, providing leadership with visibility to coverage, gaps, progress and priority actions.
Develop guidance and training to support consistent SEDEX compliance across North America Procurement.
4. Risk Decision Support and Category Enablement
Serve as the primary Procurement Risk point of contact for North America category teams and emerging risk issues, coordinating rapid assessment, stakeholder alignment and response recommendations.
Build and maintain a catalog of tools, templates and risk profiles that enable category teams to incorporate risk into category strategies, sourcing strategies, supplier reviews, SRM activities and joint business plans.
Lead regular category risk reviews, provide ad hoc guidance and troubleshooting, and drive mitigation progress against established KPIs.
Assemble cross-functional teams and create situation-specific decision frameworks to prioritize and address complex or critical risk exposures.
5. Cross-Functional Governance and Business Partnership
Lead governance routines with Supply Chain, Operations, Food Safety & Quality, R&D, Finance, Legal, Sustainability and other partners, integrating cross-functional risks that may affect supply continuity.
Partner with Business Units to prioritize critical mitigation projects, align resources and ensure the risk agenda supports strategic business objectives.
Present risk exposure, mitigation progress and priority decisions through BU performance routines and to senior Procurement and business leadership.
Strengthen procurement governance controls, monitor remediation and corrective actions, ensure compliance with policies and regulatory requirements, and support internal and external audits.
6. Digital Risk Intelligence, Data and Reporting
Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of procurement risk technologies, predictive analytics and automated monitoring capabilities.
Integrate relevant internal and external intelligence sources into risk processes and decision-making.
Build executive-ready dashboards and reporting that provide visibility to material and supplier risk exposure, mitigation pipelines, priority projects and performance against targets.
Own country-of-origin mapping capability and governance, including data refresh cadence, data ownership, collection standards, system integration and cross-functional use cases.
7. Communication, Training and Adoption
Develop and maintain annual stakeholder communication and engagement plans, including North America and Global Procurement risk updates.
Maintain the Risk Hub on Proc Connect so current tools, templates, guidance and training materials are accessible and ready for use.
Develop and deliver training on material and supplier risk, and maintain playbooks, SOPs and best-practice documentation to standardize processes and enable scalable adoption.
Drive adoption of Procurement Risk tools, dashboards, templates and practices across North America Procurement and support future deployment of the methodology to other regions.
Required Qualifications
Education
Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, Procurement, Sustainability, Engineering, Operational Excellence or a related field.
Experience
6-9 years of experience in Procurement, Supply Chain, Risk Management or a related business function.
Demonstrated experience leading supplier or material risk programs and applying third-party risk management frameworks.
Experience in CPG, food manufacturing or another regulated industry preferred.
Experience implementing or managing risk technology platforms and analytics solutions.
Technical Skills
Strong knowledge of supplier and material risk management, business continuity planning, SEDEX compliance, financial risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and crisis management.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with the ability to connect data, risk exposure and business impact.
Proficiency with analytics and visualization tools; experience with Power BI, Tableau or similar platforms preferred.
Understanding of AI-enabled monitoring, automation and emerging digital risk capabilities.
Leadership & Behavioral Competencies
Acts as Procurement’s risk subject-matter expert and trusted advisor.
Influences without authority and builds alignment across senior, cross-functional stakeholders.
Communicates complex risk topics clearly and leads executive communications during disruptions.
Demonstrates strong project management, organizational and stakeholder-management skills.
Balances strategic thinking with disciplined operational execution.
Brings curiosity, sound judgment, a continuous-improvement mindset and a willingness to challenge the status quo.

title: Asset Protection & Safety Mgr
description:
What You Will Do
All Lowe’s associates deliver quality customer service while maintaining a store that is clean, safe, and stocked with the products our customers need. As an Asset Protection & Safety Manager, this means:

The Asset Protection & Safety Manager (APSM) oversees and coordinates programs and processes to minimize loss while maintaining a safe working and shopping environment.  This associate monitors and solves for criminal activities, coaches and trains associates, and oversees inventory levels to help with shrink and shortages.  The APSM may need to respond to violent altercations to keep customers and staff safe.  The Asset Protection & Safety Manager is seen as an expert on safety reports, guidelines, and regulations.

• Minimally must be able to lift 25 pounds without assistance; may lift over 25 pounds with or without assistance.

• Bachelor's Degree or higher OR High School Diploma or equivalent and 3 years of relevant work experience (e.g., retail or Asset Protection).

title: Full Time - CDL Delivery Driver
description:
Essential Functions:
Customer Service
•Provides SMART customer service at all times through the daily execution of Lowe's customer service policies, procedures and programs
•Seeks out customers to understand his/her needs and assists in locating, demonstrating, selecting, carrying, and/or loading merchandise
•Listens to and responds knowledgeably and promptly to customer and employee questions by walking them through projects when necessary
•Demonstrates sincere appreciation to customers
•Communicates information to customers regarding all stock, special order merchandise, feature benefits, application, and warranty information related to Lowe’s programs
•Contacts customers regarding delivery or coordinates with the truck driver to call the customer
In-stock
•Plans delivery activities, prints loading tickets, and delivers merchandise according to schedule to ensure on-time delivery of orders
•Pulls merchandise, builds and bands delivery loads, and loads trucks (within payload) according to delivery order
•Inspects condition of products (e.g., appliances) before loading for delivery or assisting customer with loading
•Matches items on invoice with quantities loaded by verifying descriptions, items, and model numbers
Clean and Safe Stores
•Ensures that the loads are safe, secure, and within Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations
•Updates delivery and route status (e.g., on-site, completed) on system (e.g., iPhone) for tracking purposes
•Unloads, installs, and tests appliances upon delivery
•Verifies daily vehicle inspections and reports and ensures cleanliness, maintenance, and repairs for delivery vehicles and other equipment (e.g., lift gates)
•Completes Department of Transportation (DOT) reporting to maintain DOT certification and CDL compliance
•Detects common signs of shoplifting, theft, and other security risks, and promptly communicates them to management and/or Asset Protection
•Ensures compliance with housekeeping standards and programs (e.g., Zone Recovery) to maintain cleanliness and organization of store and working areas
•Maintains a safe and secure work environment, which may include conducting daily safety reviews, noting hazards, keeping aisles clear, and securing doors and gates
•Adheres to all safety requirements relevant to one’s regular job duties: top stock safety, reinstalling safety cables, use of aisle blockers, a tether line on power equipment, spotters, and safety devices
•Operates store equipment as needed depending on one specific role and department (e.g., Zebra phone, telephone, paging system, copiers, fax machines, computers, CCTV surveillance system, key cutter, panel saw, paint mixer, flooring cutters, compacter baler)
•In addition to the above responsibilities, this individual is held accountable for other duties as assigned
Minimum Requirements:
•Class A CDL License - In locations with multi-unit CMV (tractor trailer & flatbed) a class A license is required to operate.
or
•Class B CDL License - In locations with single-unit CMV (tandem flatbed) a class A or B license with air break endorsement is required to operate.
and
•Valid medical certificate or ability to obtain one upon employment
and
•Ability to pass MVR screen in accordance with company requirements.
and
•Ability to obtain sales related licensure or registration as may be required by law
•Ability to read, write, and perform basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction)
•Must be 21 years of age
•Ability to comply with DOT and CDL regulations
Preferences:
•1 Year Experience driving a semi-truck/trailer or certification from a driving school
•6 Months Experience performing in-home delivery or retail customer service
•3 Months Experience operating a forklift or Moffett onloading/offloading a vehicle
