description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE IDEAL CANDIDATE:
The Manager, Return to Vendor (RTV) is a key individual contributor within the Sourcing organization responsible for overseeing the end-to-end RTV process across the company's retail and e-commerce supply chain. This role serves as the primary point of contact for vendor return negotiations, disputes, and recovery, ensuring that defective, excess, and non-conforming merchandise is resolved efficiently and that the company maximizes recovery value. The ideal candidate is highly analytical, a skilled negotiator, and comfortable operating cross-functionally with Merchandising, Quality, Logistics, Finance, and Vendor partners.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
RTV Program Ownership
Own and manage the full RTV lifecycle — from claim initiation through resolution, credit receipt, or physical return logistics.
Establish and maintain a centralized RTV tracking system; monitor open claims, aging balances, and recovery rates.
Develop and enforce RTV policies, standard operating procedures, and escalation protocols.
Partner with Buying and Planning teams to identify and prioritize RTV candidates across categories.
Vendor Negotiation & Relationship Management
Lead direct negotiations with vendor partners to secure credits, replacements, or return authorizations in alignment with contractual terms.
Build and maintain productive vendor relationships while assertively advocating for the company's financial interests.
Review and interpret vendor contracts and purchase order terms related to returns, defects, and chargebacks.
Identify recurring quality or compliance issues with vendors and escalate to the Sourcing Director for strategic action.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with the Logistics and Warehouse teams to coordinate physical return shipments, disposition of goods, and inbound/outbound documentation.
Partner with Finance and Accounts Payable to ensure timely posting of vendor credits and accurate reconciliation of RTV balances.
Work with the Quality Assurance team to document and report on product defect trends to inform future sourcing decisions.
Support Buying teams during vendor onboarding to ensure RTV terms and expectations are clearly defined.
Reporting & Continuous Improvement
Produce regular reporting on RTV volume, recovery rate, aging claims, and open liabilities for senior leadership review.
Identify process gaps and implement improvements to reduce cycle time, increase recovery, and minimize dispute resolution time.
Benchmark RTV performance against industry standards and recommend best practices.
REQUIREMENTS:
5+ years of experience in sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or supply chain — with direct RTV, chargeback, or vendor compliance exposure.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with vendor partners, including knowledge of contract terms, credit processes, and dispute resolution.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to manage large volumes of data and derive actionable insights.
Proficiency in Google Sheets; experience with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or equivalent) and inventory/order management platforms.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence without authority across internal teams and external partners.
Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple open claims and priorities simultaneously.

This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary This position is tailored for an experienced, high-level Senior Field Service Technician who will serve as a technical expert and leader in supporting complex vehicle repairs and field operations. The role requires an adaptable, team-oriented leader capable of driving continuous improvement, mentoring junior team members, and tackling complex diagnostic challenges in a fast-paced environment. While based primarily at a service center, this role may involve operating remotely, traveling to remote locations, or working at production plants to provide advanced field support as business needs demand. Candidates will be evaluated against a comprehensive spectrum of advanced technical skills and leadership capabilities. Responsibilities Advanced Diagnostics & Complex Repairs: Perform bumper-to-bumper diagnostics, complex repairs, installations, and inspections on vehicles both inside service centers and in field settings (customer sites, mobile routes, or remote locations). Technical Support & Remote Troubleshooting: Provide high-level diagnostic guidance to field service teams and perform remote diagnostics or repairs for issues that can be safely addressed without local vehicle access by evaluating logged vehicle data and technical schematics. Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and train junior technicians and internal partners; foster cross-functional collaboration and lead shop-floor technical problem-solving. Advanced Tools & Methodologies: Utilize specialized diagnostic tools (e.g., PICO-Scope, PCAN, Kavaser Memorator, breakout boxes) to resolve complex electrical, high-voltage, and network faults. Quality & Process Standardization: Conduct thorough road tests to verify repair quality, champion continuous improvement processes, and drive high standards across repair workflows. Parts Operations & Systems: Oversee complex parts operations—including ordering, receiving, inventory management, and billing—to ensure quality and operational efficiency. Documentation & Technical Feedback: Produce high-quality documentation in service support and engineering systems; provide root-cause analysis and actionable feedback to field service engineers and leadership. Customer & Cross-Functional Engagement: Interact professionally with customers, suppliers, and internal teams during escalation resolutions or mobile outreach events. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school or vocational program preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including weekends, holidays, early morning, evening, or overnight shifts as required. Ability to travel to regional locations or production plants as needed. Proficient in Windows/Mac environments, work order management systems, and specialized engineering/diagnostic documentation systems. Physical capability to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). State mechanic certifications where required by jurisdiction (e.g., Michigan certifications in front end, suspension, steering, brakes, electrical, and HVAC). Experience & Leadership: 5 to 8+ years of automotive repair experience preferred, with extensive experience in bumper-to-bumper diagnostics. 3 to 8+ years of hands-on experience working on vehicle High Voltage (HV) systems and HV diagnostic work. Experience in leadership or supervisory roles (e.g., Shop Foreman, Team Lead, or Technical Mentor) preferred. Demonstrated background in continuous improvement, process standardization, and escalation management. Spectrum of Advanced Technical Skills: High Voltage (HV) & Power Electronics: Deep understanding of high-voltage architecture, High-Voltage Interlock Loops (HVIL), charging isolation, and safety power-down protocols using appropriate PPE. Capable of diagnosing complex HV faults and isolation issues. Low Voltage & Network Electronics: Advanced knowledge of automotive electronics, CAN and LIN bus network communication, reading/leveraging electrical schematics, and performing precise wiring harness repairs. Chassis, Drivability & Dynamic Systems: Mastery in chassis service (alignments, braking systems) and advanced diagnosis of vehicle dynamics (ABS, traction control, power steering, and Noise, Vibration, and Harshness / NVH concerns). Thermal & HVAC Systems: Comprehensive knowledge of HVAC systems, coolant drain/fill operations, A/C machine usage, 609 refrigerant certification, and diagnosing complex thermal management issues. ADAS & Body/Glass Integration: Proficiency in calibrating Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and replacing/adjusting sensors, body panels, and glass to precise manufacturer tolerances. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus. Field Service Technicians on the night shift will receive a 20% hourly shift differential on top of base hourly pay between the hours of 6PM-6AM. Night shift hours vary by location. Execute welding operations to join, fabricate, and repair metal and other weldable material.
Set up and operate manual and semi-automatic (robotic) welding equipment.
Read and interpret blueprints, diagrams, specifications, and job orders to determine appropriate welding processes.
Ensure welding is completed to the required standards and specifications.
Inspect welded surfaces and structures to identify defects and ensure conformity with specifications. Deburr pieces to create appropriate welding services when necessary.
Maintain welding equipment in good working condition.
Work collaboratively with team members and other departments to achieve production goals.
Record and report production data accurately and timely.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance welding processes.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
Other responsibilities as assigned.

High school diploma
1-2 years of demonstrated experience in a welding role in a manufacturing, automotive, or related environment. Or completion of a recognized welding apprenticeship program.
Proficient understanding of welding techniques, metallurgy, and welding symbols.
Knowledge of safety standards related to welding and metalworking.
Familiarity with the properties and characteristics of metals used in welding.
Understanding of welding equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
Ability to perform MIG welding techniques.
Proficient in reading and interpreting blueprints, drawings, and specifications.
Good attention to detail to ensure precision in welding tasks.
Excellent hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity.
Ability to set up, operate, and maintain welding equipment and tools.
Good problem-solving skills to identify and resolve welding-related issues.
Effective communication skills to collaborate with team members and supervisors.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Low Posture: Infrequently required to perform tasks using a low posture including but not limited to stooping, bending, crawling, crouching, kneeling or squatting

title: Core Enterprise Account Executive EST/CST - Remote
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
As a Core AE, you will be helping our largest and most strategic enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US and requires working in EST and CST timezone.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
In this role, you will:
Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Minimum requirements for the role:
5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $100k+ ARR transactions
Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships
Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting
Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast paced environment
Willing and comfortable traveling to meet customers on a monthly basis
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience working with line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)
Passion for the world of operations!
The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.
Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.
Annual OTE Salary $222,400 — $278,000 USD Total Rewards
At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.
Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.
Flexible Working
At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.
Belonging at Samsara
At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.
Accommodations
Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.
Our Commitment to Authenticity
We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.
Fraudulent Employment Offers
Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our  blog post here .

Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and argue for the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Own the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.

8+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , You have delivered reliable firmware where memory, processing power, energy and timing are all scarce, and you know how to measure, optimize and make deliberate trade-offs between them.
You have led firmware development for several new products end to end. You have taken firmware from initial concept through architecture, technical implementation, validation, and product launch, providing hands-on technical leadership throughout.
Substantial bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have brought up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Senior-level scope. You have led work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have consistently driven consensus across teams.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you make that trade-off on purpose.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping badly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.

BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

title: CV/ML Camera Test Engineer
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring a hands-on CV/ML camera test engineer to measure how camera and optics choices affect the performance of our AI models. Working with our Optics & Camera Engineering Lead, this individual will turn experiment plans into lab and field setups, run the campaigns, push the data through our CV/ML models and report what changed and why. The work is scientific at its core: reason from first principles about optics, sensor physics and illumination, form a hypothesis, design a controlled experiment to test it, and let the data decide. This individual will collaborate with camera, CV/ML, software, hardware and field teams to put data behind every camera decision.

Responsibilities:

 - Form testable hypotheses from first principles (optics, sensor physics, radiometry and illumination), and design controlled experiments with defined variables, controls, sample sizes and success criteria before collecting data.

 - Execute experiments comparing sensors, lenses, ISP settings, IR illumination, focus and window conditions, and measure their effect on detection, recognition and LPR performance at range.

 - Build and maintain lab and outdoor test setups, including targets at known distances, controlled lighting and low-light scenes, IR illumination and chamber runs across temperature.

 - Run field data-collection campaigns across sites, times of day, lighting and weather, keeping conditions, metadata and ground truth consistent.

 - Run captured video through existing CV/ML models and evaluation tools, and compute model metrics alongside image-quality measurements (MTF, SNR, distortion, pixels on target).

 - Script captures, camera settings, data pipelines and analysis in Python and shell on embedded Linux devices so every run is reproducible.

 - Isolate the cause of performance changes across optics, sensor, ISP, illumination and environment, using statistical analysis rather than anecdote, and write clear reports that state confidence, limitations and recommendations.

 - Support camera validation (focus stability, thermal, condensation, IR range) through EVT, DVT and PVT.



Qualifications:

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and being scrappy.

 - Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent.

 - 2+ years of experience in hardware test, validation or experimental work.

 - Strong Linux command line proficiency (required), including SSH, logs, file and process management and shell scripting on embedded devices.

 - Proficient in Python for scripting, data processing and analysis.

 - A scientific, first-principles mindset: you reason from the physics to predict results, design controlled experiments to test those predictions, and change your mind when the data says so.

 - Hands-on with test setups and lab equipment, and comfortable doing outdoor field work, including at night and in bad weather.

 - Strong grounding in statistics and experimental design, including hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, variance, sample sizing and trends across campaigns.

 - Exceptional organization and communication skills (both written and oral).

 - No CV/ML background required. You'll use our existing models and evaluation tools and learn the rest on the job.



Nice to Have

 - Experience with cameras, image sensors, lenses or image-quality testing (MTF, SNR, low light, IR).

 - Exposure to computer vision tools (OpenCV) or ML evaluation metrics such as precision and recall.

 - Experience with video tooling such as FFmpeg, GStreamer or V4L2.

 - Experience with thermal chambers, reliability or production test.

 - Background in physics, optics or a research lab environment.


Tool Proficiency

 - Linux command line and shell scripting (required).

 - Python with NumPy, pandas and plotting libraries.

 - Git for scripts and test procedures.

 - Imatest or equivalent image-quality tools (preferred).

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring an Optics & Camera Engineering Lead to own camera performance across our product portfolio. This individual will own the imaging stack end to end: sensor and lens selection, optical requirements tied to CV/ML and customer outcomes, vendor and JDM programs, test campaigns and results analysis, and high volume production. This individual will collaborate with systems, software, CV/ML, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain and test teams to deliver performant, scalable and validated camera + optical systems to the field.

The role spans the full stack. One day you'll be benchmarking sensors and lenses for a new product. Next, you'll work with our CV/ML team to translate detection, recognition and LPR performance at range into pixel density, MTF and low-light targets, or review athermal lens designs, define a slant-edge MTF test across temperature, or analyze a wiper endurance run. You'll work with systems, software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing and supply chain, and lead technical engagements with tier-one optics and sensor suppliers.



Responsibilities:

Select sensors and lenses

 - Evaluate and select image sensors for each product, comparing low-light performance (SNR1s, QE at 850/940 nm), pixel size, resolution, frame rate, HDR, supply life and cost.

 - Select off-the-shelf lenses or specify custom designs matched to each sensor: FOV, F-number, MTF across the field, NIR correction, distortion, relative illumination and athermal behavior.

 - Evaluate and select the ISP architecture (on-sensor, companion ASIC/FPGA or SoC ISP), weighing image quality, latency, power, cost and supply, and drive ISP tuning and pipeline development for day and NIR night modes.

 - Benchmark sensor and lens candidates side by side in the lab and the field, and keep a qualified roster of sensors, lenses and IR-cut filters ready for new programs.

Connect customer value to optical requirements

 - Translate customer use cases and CV/ML performance into camera requirements using pixel-density frameworks such as IEC 62676-4 DORI.

 - Run coverage and range trade studies across sensor resolution, FOV, mounting height, pixel density, IR range, inference load, power and cost.

 - Define MTF, aperture, distortion, relative illumination, stray light and NIR focus targets, and tie them to measured model precision and recall at distance.

 - Design and run real-world field test campaigns across sites, lighting and weather, and use the resulting model and image-quality data to close the loop from camera change to quantified customer impact and drive design decisions.

Own optical and camera system design

 - Own optical performance specifications for fixed, multi-camera, panoramic and PTZ products.

 - Integrate the selected sensor, lens, IR-cut filter and mount into a camera system that meets spec across every operating condition.

 - Drive athermal design so focus and MTF hold across a wide operating range under solar loading, accounting for IR-cut filters, lens mounts, flange CTE, humidity and pressure.

 - Specify NIR illumination (LED and laser) matched to lens FOV, including frame-synced strobing, IEC 60825-1 eye safety, thermal limits and internal-reflection control.

 - Guide window, coating, heater, wiper and sun-shade design so optical performance survives years of outdoor service.

 - Use optical simulation to evaluate concepts quickly and review supplier prescriptions with confidence.

Lead vendor and JDM programs

 - Own the technical content of RFPs for camera modules and complete camera systems, and evaluate proposals on performance, cost, schedule and risk.

 - Lead technical work with optics suppliers and ODM/JDM partners on off-the-shelf selection, custom lens design, active alignment and production test.

 - Hold partners to design reviews and gate criteria from design through EVT, DVT and PVT.

Build test capability and run campaigns

 - Grow Specter's optical lab: collimators, slant-edge MTF, focus through temperature, flare and stray light, low-light SNR, IR range and FOV/distortion measurement.

 - Design and qualify optical test equipment for development, reliability and manufacturing, with documented gauge R&R.

 - Plan and run lab reliability and qualification campaigns covering thermal, humidity, condensation, solar loading, ingress, cleaning and coating endurance, and field life, then analyze results and drive decisions.

 - Define calibration (intrinsics, extrinsics, per-unit data) and production acceptance tests at our contract manufacturers.

Scale to production and grow the team

 - Take camera systems from concept to volume production with partners and CMs, driving design for manufacturability, automated focus and alignment, and yield.

 - Partner with embedded imaging engineers on sensor bring-up, driver integration and day/night switching in production.

 - Mentor engineers across camera, image quality, test and manufacturing engineering.

 - Track emerging imaging technology (large-format sensors, zoom optics, EO/IR fusion, camera arrays, computational imaging) and recommend where Specter should invest.



Qualifications:

 - 8+ years in optical, imaging or camera systems engineering, with multiple camera products shipped to volume production.

 - Fluency across the stack, from how image quality affects CV/ML and the end user down to lens design, mechanics and test.

 - Deep knowledge of image sensors, lens design and the trade-offs among resolution, FOV, F-number, MTF, aberrations, depth of focus and thermal stability.

 - Hands-on optical simulation with Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or similar.

 - A track record specifying off-the-shelf and custom lenses with suppliers, with clear performance and cost trade-offs.

 - Athermalization experience covering both mechanical design and optical performance across temperature (focus shift, MTF drift).

 - Experience designing optical test equipment and running test campaigns, with rigorous data analysis behind decisions.

 - Experience with NIR imaging and active illumination, as well as L/M/SWIR systems.

 - Experience taking hardware through NPI with contract manufacturers or ODM/JDM partners.

 - Clear communication of optical trade-offs to software, business and customer-facing teams.



Nice to Have

 - Active alignment and high-volume camera module manufacturing.

 - PTZ, zoom/focus optics, panoramic or multi-camera systems, and camera calibration for computer vision.

Tool Proficiency

title: Senior Quality Inspector (Electronics)
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots builds AI-native industrial robot arms deployed at manufacturing facilities across the U.S. In June 2026 we closed a $200M Series C at a $1B valuation, led by RoboStrategy with continued backing from General Catalyst and new participation from the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund and Samsung Next.


About the role

Every robot we ship has to actually work — for years, in real factories, under real load. That comes down to what happens on the inspection bench before it ever leaves the building. As Senior Electronic Inspector, you're the final word on whether our PCBAs, cables, and harnesses meet the bar, and you're the person other inspectors turn to when the standard gets tricky.


What you'll do

- Inspect PCBA and electronic assemblies against IPC-A-610 acceptability criteria

- 5+ years of electronic inspection experience in a manufacturing QC environment

- Solid ESD knowledge and hands-on experience running or supporting an ESD program

- Ability to read schematics and electronic assembly drawings fluently, not just reference them

description:
Job Summary and Mission
At Starbucks, our mission is to inspire and nurture the human spirit - one person, one cup, and one neighborhood at a time. Starbucks Technologists work to achieve this mission through the use of cutting-edge technology delivered to our partners, customers, stores, roasters, and global communities.
This senior technical product manager will help shape and deliver technology that supports the operation and evolution of our coffeehouses. The role partners across business and technology teams to simplify complex workflows, modernize platforms, connect data and systems, and create intuitive experiences for partners and the teams that support our stores.
The successful candidate combines strong technical product management, platform and integration experience, and practical delivery leadership. Experience with coffeehouse or retail facilities, repair and maintenance, field service, supplier ecosystems, or other operational technology domains is a plus, but the role requires the versatility to work across a broader portfolio. The candidate should also bring experience with AI-assisted development and know how to translate emerging capabilities into secure, scalable, measurable products.
Summary of Key Responsibilities
Own product strategy, roadmap, priorities, and measurable outcomes for a portfolio of technology supporting coffeehouse operations and enabling capabilities.
Lead product planning and day-to-day decision making with business stakeholders, architects, engineering, UX, data, security, QA, operations, and other partner teams.
Translate complex operational workflows and user needs into clear product requirements and scalable technical solutions.
Lead product definition and delivery for custom enterprise applications and modernization initiatives, balancing business continuity, technical evolution, user experience, and adoption.
Identify opportunities to apply AI and automation to simplify work, improve decision making, and create better partner and operational experiences.
Apply AI-assisted and specification-driven development practices to improve requirement quality, accelerate delivery, strengthen traceability, and maintain alignment from business intent through implementation and validation.
Create and maintain product specifications, process and data flows, functional and technical requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, nonfunctional requirements, and release readiness criteria.

Ensure engineering and QA have the context needed to estimate, build, test, release, and support features, including expected behaviors, edge cases, interfaces, and success measures.
Prioritize the backlog and roadmap using customer and partner value, business outcomes, operational risk, data, architecture needs, and delivery capacity.
Coordinate modernization, migration, integration transition, cutover, and change-management activities when evolving critical operational capabilities.
Define product performance, adoption, reliability, and effectiveness measures and use insights to drive continuous improvement.
Identify and resolve delivery blockers, escalate risks early, and coordinate mitigation across business and technology teams.
Build strong relationships and communicate clearly with senior business and technology stakeholders and external partners.
Coach and mentor team members on technical product management, product discovery, specification quality, delivery practices, and outcome-based planning.
Stay current on AI, cloud technology, operational platforms, product delivery practices, and emerging capabilities; recommend innovations that are practical, secure, and aligned to business goals.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in a related field.
7+ years of industry experience in a technology environment with a record of successfully delivering complex products.
5+ years of hands-on product management experience developing roadmaps, priorities, product specifications, features, user stories, acceptance criteria, and refined backlogs in a fast-paced environment with varied stakeholders.
5+ years of experience partnering with design, architecture, engineering, and QA to deliver user-facing or enterprise workflow capabilities.
Demonstrated technical acumen across end-to-end application architecture, APIs, integrations, cloud platforms, data flows, security, testing, and production operations.
Demonstrated ability to use analytics, operational insights, and product measures to inform prioritization and product decisions.
Experience leading cross-functional delivery, managing technical dependencies, resolving ambiguity, and influencing outcomes without direct authority.
Experience with agile product development practices and modern product discovery, delivery, and lifecycle-management tools.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with technology supporting coffeehouse, retail, restaurant, or other distributed physical operations.
Experience with facilities, repair and maintenance, field service, work order management, asset management, supplier/service-provider workflows, or adjacent operational domains.
Experience delivering custom cloud applications and API-based integrations; Microsoft Azure experience is a plus.
Experience modernizing or replacing critical enterprise platforms, including discovery, process redesign, data migration, integration transition, change management, cutover, and adoption.
Hands-on experience with AI-assisted software development and specification-driven development, including translating product intent into
structured specifications that support engineering, testing, and traceability.
Experience defining AI-enabled product capabilities, including appropriate human review, privacy, security, data quality, evaluation, monitoring, and measurable business value.
Ability to read and understand code, API contracts, technical designs, data models, and engineering specifications; prior software development experience is a plus.
Ability to understand complex business and technical issues, make clear tradeoffs, and communicate decisions to technical and nontechnical audiences.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities.
Experience collaborating with external vendors or suppliers while maintaining clear product ownership and accountability.

We believe in creating a warm and welcoming space where every cup of coffee sparks connection.   As a coffeehouse leader, you don’t just run a business—you lead a team that creates moments of connection and joy.    Every day provides an opportunity to lead with craft and heart, making your coffeehouse a place where your community feels welcome.
We are invested in your growth journey, empowered through developmental experiences as well as our industry leading benefits .
We'd love to hear from people with:
3 years retail / customer service management experience or 4+ years of US Military service
Strong organizational, interpersonal and problem solving skills
Entrepreneurial mentality with experience in a sales focused environment
Strong leadership skills and the ability to coach and mentor team partners with professional maturity
Minimum High School or GED
Requirements:
Legal documentation establishing your identity and eligibility to be legally employed in the country in which you apply.
Ability to work full time (the work regularly demands in excess of 40 hours per week) including variable hours including early mornings, evenings, weekends and/ or holidays.
Let us give you the opportunity to grow as an individual, to build lasting relationships and make an impact in a place where people, quality and value mean everything.
Join us and connect with something bigger, apply today!
As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. Starbucks also offers eligible partners participation in a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match, a discounted company stock program (S.I.P.), Starbucks equity program (Bean Stock), incentivized emergency savings, and financial well-being tools.  Additionally, Starbucks offers 100% upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor’s degree through Arizona State University’s online program via the Starbucks College Achievement Plan, student loan management resources, and access to other educational opportunities.  You will also have access to backup care and DACA reimbursement.   Starbucks will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, and in accordance with its plans and policies. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com .
*If you are working in CA, CO, IL, LA, ME, MA, NE, ND or RI, you will accrue vacation up to a maximum of 120 hours (190 in CA) for roles below director and 200 hours (316 in CA) for roles at director or above.  For roles in other states, you will be granted vacation time starting at 120 hours annually for roles below director and 200 hours annually for roles director and above.
The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, and internal equity.  At Starbucks, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate.

title: Account Executive - Bridge
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the Team
The Account Management team at Bridge is dedicated to the growth, retention, and expansion of key customers. Our Scaled Account Management team focuses on driving measurable expansion across a broad portfolio of mid-market and high-growth customers through data-driven strategies, efficient processes, and strong cross-functional partnership.
What You'll Do
As a Scaled Account Manager at Bridge you will own a book of existing accounts and be responsible for expanding revenue, identifying product gaps and driving product adoption, preventing churn and ensuring renewals at scale. You will combine consultative selling with volume playbooks, prioritization based on quantitative signals, and hands-on execution to identify and close upsell opportunities across your territory. As Bridge continues to develop within Stripe’s Money Management organization, you will also drive your customers’ adoption of additional features available through Stripe.
Responsibilities
- Own a book of existing accounts and drive revenue growth through additional usage, upsells, cross-sells, and renewals.
- Develop and execute scalable go-to-market strategies that increase revenue per account and accelerate product adoption across your portfolio.
- Use data and quantitative analysis to prioritize accounts and identify the highest-impact expansion opportunities.
- Generate leads through targeted outreach, research, and campaign execution; manage high-velocity deal cycles from qualification to close.
- Build strong relationships with customer stakeholders to understand business priorities, surface pain points, and tailor Bridge solutions.
- Lead commercial negotiations and renewals to expand and retain customer revenue.
- Identify churn signals in your book and implement strategies to prevent revenue losses.
- Coordinate with product, success, risk, and operations teams to solve complex customer needs and ensure a great user experience.
- Translate customer feedback into actionable product and process improvements to better serve scaled customer segments.
Who You Are
-5–8 years of full sales cycle or account management experience focused on existing business accounts; experience managing a large book of accounts or high-velocity portfolio strongly preferred.
- Strong analytical skills with experience using data to prioritize accounts, build business cases, and track outcomes.
- Comfortable understanding technical product requirements and articulating solutions across multiple technology products.
- Demonstrated ability to close upsell opportunities and manage complex pricing or commercial negotiations.
- Excellent operational acumen and proven ability to manage time and prioritize across a high-volume territory.
- Highly motivated, persistent, and effective in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
- Superior written and verbal communication skills.
- Willingness and ability to work in-office in New York or San Francisco at least three days per week.
Preferred Qualifications
- Previous experience at a high-growth payments, fintech, crypto, or technology company.
- Experience with CRM tools, Excel, and basic SQL or a demonstrated comfort with data tools and analysis.
- Background in working cross-functionally with product, risk, and operations teams to deliver outcomes for customers.
Why Bridge
Join a team that values clear thinking, quantitative rigor, and customer obsession. At Bridge you’ll own meaningful customer outcomes, operate with autonomy, and have the opportunity to shape how we scale revenue across high-potential accounts.

Revenue Recognition is our first major proof point. Stripe has a unique opportunity to help Billing and Metronome users turn complex revenue activity—including usage-based pricing, minimum commitments, credits, and contract modifications—into accurate, explainable journal entries. Our ambition is for agents to take on the investigation, configuration, and repetitive work while accountants retain control over consequential judgments and approvals.

Scripts — Secure, isolated TypeScript runtime allowing merchants and developers to customize Stripe product behavior (e.g., discount calculations, invoice logic, proration).

Workflows — A programmable orchestration layer (graduating to GA at Sessions) enabling no-code and pro-code business logic across Stripe, including custom actions, delays, smart retries, and 3P integrations.

The UL Solutions Research and Development team is seeking a driven and team-oriented laboratory technician to work with us on research and testing of emerging fire and explosion safety problems. Many of these problems will focus on the energy and fire protection industries, including lithium-ion battery thermal runaway and fires in the built environment. This role will focus on laboratory testing, logistics, and the design, realization and commissioning of novel test programs, fixtures and apparatus. Day-to-day projects will involve working with R&D engineers and senior lab staff to design and execute custom test programs and services for internal and external clients. Successful candidate will be creative, curious, adaptable to a fast-paced and multi-disciplined environment and able to work collaboratively with a team of other technicians, engineers and scientists to solve complex problems.
Provides technical support in the design and construction of test fixtures, test rooms or systems and other testing programs.
Designs, adapts and builds test setups and equipment for new test situations, based on analysis of test specifications and discussions with engineers.
Examines test samples and interprets measuring instruments, blueprints, schematics, wiring diagrams, and operational instructions.
Develops test procedures based on laboratory procedures, standards and safety policies.
Engages in firefighting and fire extinguishing activities in live fire tests under supervision of more senior technician staff.
Sets and operates data acquisition suites for custom test scenarios.
Assists in scheduling, assigning, reviewing and coordinating workflow to assure proper utilization of laboratory time and space.
Can operate with minimal supervision within defined limits of responsibility.
Attends meetings and uses multiple forms of communication, as needed, to complete tasks, projects, and initiatives
Prepares purchase and material requisitions.
Takes stewardship over laboratory spaces to ensure they remain clean, organized, operational, and up-to-date.
Integrates continuous improvement concepts and techniques into all aspects of the job.
Highschool diploma or GED required
At least 2-year university degree in engineering or a related discipline is preferred
Prior experience in hands-on laboratory work and mechanical design/assembly work is required
Qualifications to operate a forklift, boom lift, and scissor lift.
Willingness to be trained in and to engage in active firefighting in full turn-out gear. This requires the ability to maintain composure and make clear and rapid decisions in an Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH) fire environment.
Ability to obtain self-container breathing apparatus (SCBA) certification. Existing certification is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects while maintaining high quality and exceptional customer service.
Demonstrated hands-on experience using and safely operating a variety of hand tools and power tools.
Highly effective communication skills and ability to interact with customers
Demonstrated project experience involving creative problem solving.
Desire to work in a team-oriented environment
What you’ll experience working for ULS
UL Solutions has been pioneering change since 1894 and we’re still leading the way. From day one, we’ve blazed a trail protecting the planet and everyone on it. Our teams have influenced billions of products, plus services, software offerings and more. We break things, burn things and blow things up. All in the name of safety science.

Remix is Via's premier transit planning and scheduling platform, trusted by transit agencies worldwide to design networks, model scenarios, and optimize service. We're looking for a Director of Product to define and drive the next era of Remix: a multimodal planning and scheduling system that gives transit agencies a single, authoritative place to make smarter decisions across every service type they operate.
This is a high-impact, high-ownership role. You will shape the vision for how agencies move from static schedules to data-driven, dynamically optimized operations — balancing labor union rules and contractual constraints with the operational agility modern transit demands. You will own the end-to-end product experience from strategic planning through live execution, and your work will directly affect how millions of riders experience public transit every day.

Define and own the product vision and roadmap for Remix as the global standard for multimodal transit planning and scheduling, spanning fixed route, paratransit, microtransit, and emerging modes
Build the framework for data-driven scheduling — enabling agencies to make optimal use of driver and vehicle time through intelligent analysis of ridership patterns, operational constraints, and service goals
Deeply understand and incorporate labor union rules, collective bargaining agreements, and workforce regulations into the product in a way that is structured yet flexible enough to adapt as those rules evolve
Connect planning and scheduling seamlessly to live operations, reducing the gap between what is scheduled and what is executed — improving accuracy, dispatcher confidence, and rider reliability
Partner closely with engineering, design, data science, and GTM teams to move from vision to shipped product with clear milestones and measurable outcomes
Engage directly and frequently with transit planners, schedulers, and operations leaders to surface unmet needs and validate product direction
Stay current on industry trends, emerging regulations, and competitive dynamics to keep Remix ahead of the market
Who You Are:
You have 10+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex enterprise software products
Have a track record of shipping high-quality products for sophisticated, workflow-heavy enterprise environments where the cost of getting it wrong is high
Are a systems thinker who can hold both strategic vision and operational detail — you know when to zoom out and when to get into the weeds
Have strong instincts for simplifying complexity: translating divergent customer needs and intricate business rules into clean, scalable product decisions
Bring deep empathy for the professionals who use your product daily — planners, schedulers, dispatchers — and design with their real working context in mind
Can quickly become technically fluent in the underlying data models and entities that power scheduling and operations systems — blocks, runs, trips, stops, vehicles, duties, pairings — and can engage at that level of specificity with engineers and architects
Are a strong, credible voice in technical architecture decisions alongside your engineering partners, capable of evaluating tradeoffs and advocating for platform choices that serve both current product needs and long-term scalability
Experience with resource management, labor scheduling, or workforce optimization software is a strong plus
Experience in transportation, transit, or logistics is a plus but not required — intellectual curiosity and the ability to learn technical domains quickly matter more

title: Hardware Engineer - Test Development
description:
Zoox is building a purpose-built, fully autonomous robotaxi, and every electronic control unit (ECU) on it has to be proven before it reaches a vehicle. The Autonomy Hardware Validation team in Robot Platform Verification & Validation runs the design validation (DV) and production validation (PV) testing that shows our ECUs meet their requirements across temperature, power, vibration, EMC and lifetime stress. As a Hardware Engineer on our Test Development team, you will be the hands-on engineer who gets testing done in our Foster City labs. You will build test setups and automation, run tests, and help find the root cause of failures. You will move between projects as needs shift, including next-generation vehicle platforms, production validation for our current robotaxi, and cold-weather qualification. You will use AI tools and automation to build and run tests faster. In this role, you will:
Build, debug and maintain test setups for vehicle ECUs, including fixtures, test carts, harnesses, fault injection racks, power supplies, electronic loads, data acquisition and thermal chambers.

Run electrical, environmental and reliability tests in our Foster City labs and at local test labs, and document the results clearly.
Write test automation and tools in Python, and use AI tools to review specifications and test procedures, synthesize results and speed up test development.

Support root cause analysis of test failures with validation, design, firmware and supplier quality engineers, and track issues to closure in Jira.

Add capacity where it’s needed most, working with validation leads to turn their validation plans into working test setups and procedures.
Qualifications:
  • 2+ years of experience in hardware test, hardware validation or electrical engineering, and a BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related field.
  • Hands-on experience with lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads, DMMs and data acquisition systems.
  • Experience building or modifying test setups such as harnesses, fixtures or instrumentation, and reading schematics to debug board-level issues.
  • Working proficiency in Python for test automation or data analysis.
  • Comfortable using AI tools to review documents, synthesize information and build test tooling, and checking their output critically.
  • Experience with fault injection, hardware-in-the-loop or automated test equipment for electronics.
  • Experience with automotive validation standards such as ISO 16750, CISPR 25 or ISO 11452, including EMC or cold-weather testing.
  • Experience working in Jira, Polarion or another ALM tool.
